user_story: As an administrator, I want to create cloud provider credential templates, so that I can manage provider access centrally
expected_behavior: CRUD for credential templates (AWS, Azure, GCP, IBM Cloud). Can mark as default. Fields include provider, API key/secret, region.
validation_notes: AuthTemplates.tsx renders CredentialTemplates component; backend credential_templates.py + credential_template_service.py provide full CRUD for aws/gcp/azure/ibm with is_default management and provider/region/key fields.

user_story: As a user, I want to manage SSH jumphost configurations, so that I can access on-prem resources
expected_behavior: CRUD for SSH credentials with host, port, username, key/password auth. Test connection capability.
validation_notes: AuthTemplates.tsx renders SSHCredentials component; backend ssh_credentials.py exposes CRUD with host/port/username/auth_type plus /{id}/test connection testing via SSHCredentialService.

user_story: As an operator, I want to create a new alert channel (webhook, Slack, MS Teams, email), so that alerts route to my preferred notification system.
expected_behavior: POST /api/alert-channels validates channel_type; requires url for webhook/slack/msteams; creates channel with optional event_types (health_change, drift_detected, deploy_success, deploy_failed, deploy_started) and project/cluster filters; min_interval_seconds for rate limiting.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:create_alert_channel validates channel_type against {webhook,slack,msteams,email}, requires url for webhook/slack/msteams, stores event_types/project_ids/cluster_ids/min_interval_seconds.

user_story: As an operator, I want to delete an alert channel, so that I can remove unused notification routing.
expected_behavior: DELETE /api/alert-channels/{id} deletes channel and its history; returns success.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:delete_alert_channel deletes the channel; AlertHistory removal relies on FK cascade and returns {success:true}.

user_story: As an operator, I want to view a specific alert channel configuration and recent delivery history, so that I can troubleshoot delivery issues.
expected_behavior: GET /api/alert-channels/{id} returns full channel config (url, headers, secret, event_types, filters); includes recent_history (last 20 deliveries with status/error_message/http_status_code).
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:get_alert_channel returns full config (url, headers, event_types, filters) plus recent_history limited to last 20 with status/error_message/http_status_code.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see all configured alert channels and filter by type/enabled status, so that I can review notification routing.
expected_behavior: GET /api/alert-channels lists all channels; optional filters for enabled and channel_type (webhook/slack/msteams/email); includes send/failure stats and last_fired_at.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:list_alert_channels filters by enabled and channel_type, includes total_sent/total_failed and last_fired_at via _serialize_channel.

user_story: As an operator, I want to send a test alert to verify channel configuration, so that I can confirm delivery is working.
expected_behavior: POST /api/alert-channels/{id}/test sends test alert via channel; returns success/failure with status_code and duration_ms; records delivery in history.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:test_alert_channel delegates to alert_service.test_channel which records AlertHistory and returns success/status_code/duration_ms.

user_story: As an operator, I want to enable/disable an alert channel without deleting it, so that I can temporarily suspend notifications.
expected_behavior: POST /api/alert-channels/{id}/toggle flips enabled flag; returns new state.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:toggle_alert_channel flips channel.enabled and returns new {enabled} state.

user_story: As an operator, I want to modify an alert channel configuration, so that I can adjust routing and rate limiting.
expected_behavior: PUT /api/alert-channels/{id} updates channel fields; returns updated config.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:update_alert_channel applies exclude_unset fields and returns updated serialized config.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see the delivery history for a specific channel with pagination, so that I can audit alert sending.
expected_behavior: GET /api/alert-channels/{id}/history returns paginated history (default 50, max 200) with optional filters (event_type, status); shows all delivery metadata.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:get_channel_history paginates (limit default 50, le=200) with event_type/status filters and returns total + full delivery metadata.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see recent alerts across all channels, optionally filtered by event_type/severity, so that I can review what's been firing.
expected_behavior: GET /api/alert-channels/history/recent returns recent alerts (last 20) with optional filters; shows event_type, severity, title, status, created_at.
validation_notes: alert_channels.py:get_recent_alerts defaults limit=20 (max 100) with event_type/severity filters, returns event_type/severity/title/status/created_at.

user_story: As an auditor, I want to see audit statistics for a time period (e.g., last 7 days), so that I can summarize activity.
expected_behavior: GET /api/audit/stats returns breakdown by action, resource_type, user, status; daily_activity array for charting; period configurable (1-90 days, default 7).
validation_notes: audit.py:get_audit_stats returns actions/resource_types/users/statuses breakdowns plus daily_activity; days bounded 1-90 default 7.

user_story: As a dashboard designer, I want to fetch available filter values for audit logs, so that I can populate filter dropdowns.
expected_behavior: GET /api/audit/filters returns distinct values for actions, resource_types, users, statuses; sorted alphabetically.
validation_notes: audit.py:get_audit_filters returns sorted distinct actions/resource_types/users/statuses (scoped to own logs for non-admins).

user_story: As an auditor, I want to view paginated audit logs with filtering and search, so that I can track all platform actions.
expected_behavior: GET /api/audit returns paginated logs (default 50, max 200) with filters: user, action, resource_type, resource_id, status, since, until, search; non-admins see only their own logs; ordered by timestamp desc.
validation_notes: [staging] The search filter only ILIKEs resource_name and http_path; the AuditLog.details column is not included despite the Query param docstring listing 'details'. FIX: Add `| (AuditLog.details.ilike(search_term))` to the OR clause in the search filter at backend/routes/audit.py:81-84 (cast/coerce details to text if it is a JSON/JSONB column). | WO-4 #357: audit search now covers the details column (cast to text).

user_story: As an admin, I want to create new user accounts, so that I can grant platform access to team members.
expected_behavior: Admin submits username, email, password, role (admin/operator/viewer); validates role, checks duplicate username/email, creates User with hashed password, optionally flags must_change_password. Raises ConflictError for duplicates, BadRequestError for invalid role.
validation_notes: [staging] create_user() supports a must_change_password parameter (default False), but UserCreateRequest has no such field and create_new_user never passes it, so an admin cannot set it at creation time. FIX: Add `must_change_password: bool = False` to UserCreateRequest (schemas/auth.py) and forward `must_change_password=request.must_change_password` in create_new_user's call to create_user (routes/auth.py); regenerate openapi types. | WO-4 #356: create_user honours must_change_password from the request.

user_story: As an admin, I want to remove user accounts, so that I can revoke access from departed team members.
expected_behavior: Prevents self-deletion, deletes User record, logs action. Returns success or NotFoundError; ForbiddenError if deleting self.
validation_notes: delete_user raises ForbiddenError on self-deletion, NotFoundError if missing, deletes record, commits, and logs the action with actor.

feature: Admin: List Users with Ownership Counts
user_story: As an admin, I want to see all users and how many projects each owns, so that I can manage access effectively.
expected_behavior: Single JOIN query between User and Project, aggregates project_count per user, returns all users sorted by creation date with ownership counts and metadata.
validation_notes: list_users uses a single outerjoin(Project)+group_by(User.id) query, aggregates count(Project.id) as project_count, orders by created_at, and returns users with metadata and total.

user_story: As an admin, I want to modify user details (role, email, active status), so that I can manage permissions.
expected_behavior: Partial update of role/email/is_active; prevents self-demotion from admin and self-deactivation, validates role, checks duplicate email. Raises ForbiddenError for self-demotion/deactivation, ConflictError for duplicate email.
validation_notes: update_user does partial role/email/is_active update, blocks self-demotion and self-deactivation (ForbiddenError), validates role (BadRequestError), and checks duplicate email (ConflictError).

user_story: As a user, I want to change my password, so that I can maintain account security.
expected_behavior: User provides current and new password; system verifies current against stored hash, validates new (min 8 chars), updates hashed_password, clears must_change_password. Errors if current incorrect or new too short.
validation_notes: auth_service.change_password verifies current against hash (BadRequestError if wrong), enforces min 8 chars, sets new hashed_password and clears must_change_password; route is JWT-gated and commits.

user_story: As a user, I want to retrieve my profile information, so that I can verify my identity and permissions.
expected_behavior: Endpoint validates JWT from Authorization header, retrieves User record, returns id, username, email, role, is_active, must_change_password, last_login_at. Raises UnauthorizedError if token invalid or user inactive.
validation_notes: get_me uses get_current_user → get_user_from_token, decoding JWT, loading user, raising UnauthorizedError if not found or inactive, and returns id/username/email/role/is_active/must_change_password/last_login_at.

user_story: As a system, I want to restrict project access to owners or admins, so that users cannot modify projects they don't own.
expected_behavior: Checks project.user_id against current user.id; admins bypass, non-owners get ForbiddenError. Works for project, module, and cluster ownership.
validation_notes: [staging] _check_ownership returns (allows) when project.user_id is None ('legacy projects with no owner'), so a non-owner is not denied for null-owner projects, contradicting the blanket 'non-owners get ForbiddenError' claim. FIX: Either backfill all projects with an owner and remove the `if project.user_id is None: return` bypass, or scope the bypass to admins only; to match the expected_behavior, non-owners must get ForbiddenError even for null-owner projects. | WO-4 #356 (doc): null-owner legacy projects are intentionally allowed until backfilled; non-admin denial applies to owned projects.

user_story: As a developer, I want to enforce role-based access across routes, so that permissions are consistently applied.
expected_behavior: Dependencies extract+validate JWT, check role against allowed set. require_admin needs admin; require_operator accepts admin/operator; require_viewer accepts any authenticated user. Raises ForbiddenError if insufficient.
validation_notes: require_role factory checks user.role against allowed set raising ForbiddenError; require_admin={admin}, require_operator={admin,operator}, require_viewer={admin,operator,viewer}; all flow through get_current_user JWT validation.

user_story: As a user, I want to authenticate with my username/password, so that I can access the platform securely.
expected_behavior: User submits username and password; system verifies credentials against hashed password in database, updates last_login_at, returns JWT token valid for 24 hours with username and role embedded. Returns UnauthorizedError if credentials invalid or account disabled.
validation_notes: login → authenticate_user verifies bcrypt hash (UnauthorizedError on bad creds or disabled account), updates last_login_at; create_access_token embeds sub(username)+role with 24h expiry (JWT_EXPIRATION_HOURS=24).

user_story: As a user, I want to authenticate with username and password, so that I can securely access the platform
expected_behavior: Login form with username/password fields. Supports password change on first login. Brand panel with app info and floating animations.
validation_notes: Login.tsx has username/password form with zod validation, must_change_password flow swaps to ChangePasswordForm, and BrandPanel renders app info + animate-float-slow/medium/fast shapes.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check if a backup or restore operation is currently in progress, so that I don't start conflicting operations.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/backup/status returns in_progress boolean, operation (backup/restore), started_at, message.
validation_notes: system.py:get_backup_status -> backup_service.get_backup_status reports in_progress/operation/started_at/message derived from maintenance status.

user_story: As an admin, I want to create a backup archive containing database dump and encryption key, so that I can restore if disaster strikes.
expected_behavior: POST /api/system/backup with passphrase creates .tar.gz containing pg_dump (gzipped), wrapped encryption key, metadata; returns file download; audit logs backup metadata.
validation_notes: backup_service.create_backup runs gzipped pg_dump, wraps Fernet key with passphrase, builds metadata, packages tar.gz and audit-logs; system.py:create_backup streams FileResponse.

user_story: As an admin, I want to restore a backup archive, so that I can recover the database and encryption key after data loss.
expected_behavior: POST /api/system/restore uploads .tar.gz, verifies passphrase unwraps key, enters maintenance mode (503), restores database, runs migrations, replaces encryption key, schedules backend restart.
validation_notes: backup_service.restore_backup verifies passphrase, enters maintenance mode, restores DB, runs migrations, replaces key; system.py:restore_backup schedules os._exit restart post-response. 503 enforced by maintenance_middleware.

user_story: As an operator, I want to stop an in-flight deployment, so that I can abort a failed run.
expected_behavior: POST /bare-metal/deployments/{id}/cancel sets status to cancelled, revokes Celery task.
validation_notes: cancel_deployment (orchestrator.py:654) sets status=CANCELLED, stamps completed_at, and revokes the Celery task with terminate=True; route commits.

user_story: As an operator, I want to start a bare-metal deployment to a host, so that I can provision DPU and K8s.
expected_behavior: POST /bare-metal/deployments creates plan, enqueues Celery task, returns deployment with step states.
validation_notes: create_deployment builds plan from host topology and route create_deployment (bare_metal_deployments.py:45) enqueues execute_bare_metal_deployment.delay and returns deployment with step states.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see a deployment's current status and all step results, so that I can monitor progress.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/deployments/{id} returns deployment with current_phase, current_step_index, all step results.
validation_notes: get_deployment + _deployment_to_response (bare_metal_deployments.py:184) return current_phase, current_step_index, and all sorted step results.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to download the output log from a deployment step, so that I can debug failures.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/deployments/{id}/steps/{index}/logs returns output_log, error_message, exit_code.
validation_notes: get_step_logs (bare_metal_deployments.py:154) finds the step by index and returns output_log, error_message, exit_code (404 if index missing).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all deployments for a project or host, so that I can track execution history.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/deployments returns list of BareMetalDeployment records with status, current phase, step count.
validation_notes: list_deployments returns BareMetalDeployment records mapped to responses with status, current_phase, and full step list.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see what steps will run before deploying, so that I can validate the plan.
expected_behavior: POST /bare-metal/deployments/preview returns step plan with phase breakdown, prerequisites, and prerequisite warnings.
validation_notes: preview_deployment (orchestrator.py:786) returns per-step phase, prerequisites list, idempotent flag, and prerequisite_warnings via _validate_phase_prerequisites.

user_story: As an operator, I want to resume a failed deployment from a specific step, so that I can recover without re-running earlier steps.
expected_behavior: POST /bare-metal/deployments/{id}/resume marks step as pending, re-enqueues Celery task.
validation_notes: resume_deployment (orchestrator.py:608) resets failed steps >= resume_from_step to PENDING; route resume_deployment re-dispatches execute_bare_metal_deployment.delay.

user_story: As an operator, I want to register a new bare-metal host, so that I can prepare it for deployment.
expected_behavior: POST /bare-metal/hosts creates BareMetalHost with host_ip, topology, network_mode, optional BMC/IPMI credentials.
validation_notes: create_host (host_service.py:45) persists host_ip/topology/network_mode and optionally encrypts BMC/IPMI credentials.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove a bare-metal host registration, so that I can clean up decommissioned hardware.
expected_behavior: DELETE /bare-metal/hosts/{id} removes the BareMetalHost record.
validation_notes: delete_host (host_service.py:121) removes the project-scoped BareMetalHost record; route commits.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to inspect a specific bare-metal host's configuration, so that I can see its topology and credentials.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/hosts/{id} returns full BareMetalHostResponse with SSH/BMC/IPMI creds and last discovery result.
validation_notes: [staging] The defect was a doc overstatement, not a code bug: get_host returns BareMetalHostResponse with boolean credential-presence flags (has_bmc_credentials, has_ipmi_credentials, ssh/dpu credential ids) — security-correct — and the full discovery blob is served by the separate /discovery-result endpoint. Code matches the (corrected) behavior.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to download the full discovery payload, so that I can inspect the probed topology.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/hosts/{id}/discovery-result returns full cached discovery output (BMCs, DPUs, VLAN probes) or 404.
validation_notes: get_discovery_result (bare_metal_hosts.py:147) returns host.last_discovery_result raw payload or raises NotFoundError (404) if never run.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see the last discovery run status for a host, so that I can check if it succeeded.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/hosts/{id}/discovery returns BareMetalHostResponse with last_discovery_status and error.
validation_notes: get_discovery_results (bare_metal_hosts.py:135) returns BareMetalHostResponse including last_discovery_status and last_discovery_error.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all registered bare-metal hosts in a project, so that I can browse available deployment targets.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/hosts returns list of BareMetalHost records with topology, network mode, discovery status.
validation_notes: list_hosts (host_service.py:25) returns project hosts mapped to responses carrying topology, network_mode, and last_discovery_status.

user_story: As an operator, I want to probe a bare-metal host for BMC, DPU, and VLAN topology, so that I can discover its hardware.
expected_behavior: POST /bare-metal/hosts/{id}/discover enqueues Celery task to run BMC+DPU+host probes in parallel.
validation_notes: [staging] run_discovery executes probes sequentially within one Celery task (probe_host, then probe_bmc, then probe_dpu, then probe_vlan); there is no parallel fan-out, contradicting the 'run BMC+DPU+host probes in parallel' claim. FIX: Either correct the documented behavior to 'sequential probes within one task', or refactor run_discovery to run the independent probes concurrently (e.g. ThreadPoolExecutor / Celery group) since dpu/vlan depend on host_result while bmc does not. | WO-4 #357 (doc): bare-metal discovery probes run sequentially within one Celery task.

user_story: As an operator, I want to modify a host's configuration (IPs, credentials, topology), so that I can reconfigure it.
expected_behavior: PUT /bare-metal/hosts/{id} updates host_ip, network_mode, ssh/bmc credentials, and other fields.
validation_notes: update_host (host_service.py:85) updates host_ip/network_mode and re-encrypts ssh/bmc/ipmi credentials via the field-to-encrypted-column map.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to inspect a specific version profile's compatibility requirements, so that I can validate a deployment.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/version-profiles/{id} returns BnkVersionProfileResponse with kernel, DOCA, BFB versions.
validation_notes: get_version_profile route delegates to BnkVersionProfileService.get_profile returning BnkVersionProfileResponse with kernel/DOCA/BFB version fields.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all BNK version profiles (DPU OS + host kernel compatibility), so that I can choose one.
expected_behavior: GET /bare-metal/version-profiles returns list of BnkVersionProfile with version matrix and compatibility notes.
validation_notes: list_version_profiles (bare_metal_version_profiles.py:21) returns the version-matrix profile list via BnkVersionProfileService.list_profiles.

user_story: As a performance analyst, I want to compare multiple benchmark runs side-by-side to evaluate proxy performance differences.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/compare takes run_ids array; returns normalized metrics comparison (latency, throughput, success rate) across runs.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:compare_benchmark_runs -> benchmark_service.compare_runs takes run_ids and returns normalized cross-run metric comparison.

user_story: As a benchmark operator, I want to deploy a proxy (envoy, nginx, haproxy) to a K8s cluster via Helm, so that I can route traffic through it.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/targets/{id}/proxies creates ProxyDeployment record (status=pending), dispatches Celery Helm install task, returns celery_task_id; frontend polls for status updates.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:deploy_proxy creates ProxyDeployment (pending), dispatches deploy_proxy_task.delay, stores celery_task_id for polling.

user_story: As a benchmark operator, I want to auto-discover LLM inference services on a K8s cluster, so that I can quickly create benchmark targets.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/discover-targets scans cluster for vLLM, TGI, LiteLLM, Ollama services by labels/ports/images; auto-creates BenchmarkTarget records; optionally runs proxy discovery.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:discover_targets -> target_discovery_service.discover_targets scans cluster for LLM services, auto-creates targets and optionally runs proxy discovery.

user_story: As a benchmark operator, I want to scan a cluster for existing proxies (envoy, nginx, haproxy, f5-bnk, nodeport), so that I can use them for testing.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/targets/{id}/discover-proxies discovers all proxy types in parallel; auto-creates ProxyDeployment records with status=discovered for found proxies.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:discover_proxies -> proxy_discovery_service.discover_all scans proxy types and auto-creates ProxyDeployment status=discovered.

user_story: As a test engineer, I want to push load test results from aiperf CLI into Forge, so that results are centralized and comparable.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/results ingests canonical BenchmarkResult JSON; POST /api/benchmarks/results/aiperf accepts raw aiperf export with optional query params (proxy, model, url, agent_name, run_label); stores denormalized metrics.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:ingest_benchmark_result and ingest_aiperf_result (with proxy/model/url/agent_name/run_label query params) store denormalized metrics via benchmark_service.

user_story: As a test engineer, I want to list, view, create, and cancel benchmark runs, so that I can orchestrate load tests.
expected_behavior: GET/POST /api/benchmarks/runs lists runs with filters (proxy, tool, model, status); POST creates new run; GET /{run_id} includes full result_json; POST /{run_id}/cancel stops running tests; DELETE removes run data.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py list/create/get/cancel/delete benchmark run endpoints all present with documented filters; get returns full result_json via BenchmarkRunDetailResponse.

user_story: As a benchmark operator, I want to register K8s clusters and LLM endpoints as benchmark targets, so that proxies can route traffic to them.
expected_behavior: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/benchmarks/targets manages targets (cluster_id, llm_base_url, llm_model, llm_endpoint); POST /validate tests connectivity and updates status.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py full target CRUD plus validate_benchmark_target that tests connectivity and updates status.

user_story: As a dashboard client, I want to poll the status of a proxy deploy/undeploy operation, so that I can show real-time progress.
expected_behavior: GET /api/benchmarks/targets/{id}/proxies/{proxy_id}/task-status returns ProxyDeployment with status (pending/deploying/ready/uninstalled/failed), proxy_url, celery_task_id, and Celery state.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:get_proxy_task_status returns ProxyDeployment status/proxy_url/celery_task_id and the live Celery AsyncResult state.

user_story: As a benchmark operator, I want to redeploy a proxy after configuration changes, so that new settings take effect.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/targets/{id}/proxies/{proxy_id}/redeploy resets status to pending, dispatches new Helm install task.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:redeploy_proxy resets status to pending via service then dispatches fresh deploy_proxy_task.

user_story: As a test infrastructure owner, I want to register test client machines (aiperf instances) and track their connectivity status.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/agents registers agent by name; GET /api/benchmarks/agents lists agents with status (connected/disconnected/running); agents connect via WebSocket to receive commands.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py register/list/get/delete agent endpoints present; agents connect via /ws/benchmarks/agents/{id} which flips status connected/running/disconnected.

user_story: As a test engineer, I want to save and reuse benchmark run configurations, so that I can standardize test parameters across runs.
expected_behavior: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/benchmarks/configs manage saved RunConfig presets; config_json field contains full aiperf CLI parameters.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py config CRUD endpoints manage RunConfig presets; config_json holds full aiperf parameters.

feature: Trigger Benchmark Run Against Deployed Proxy
user_story: As a performance analyst, I want to trigger a load test against a deployed proxy, so that I can measure its performance.
expected_behavior: POST /api/benchmarks/targets/{id}/proxies/{proxy_id}/run validates proxy ready status, resolves agent, builds RunConfig from target info, creates BenchmarkRun, sends command to agent via WebSocket.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:trigger_benchmark_run validates proxy ready/discovered, resolves agent, builds config_json from target, creates BenchmarkRun, sends run command via send_command_to_agent WebSocket.

user_story: As a benchmark operator, I want to remove a deployed proxy via Helm uninstall, so that I can clean up after testing.
expected_behavior: DELETE /api/benchmarks/targets/{id}/proxies/{proxy_id} (202 Accepted) dispatches async Helm uninstall task; if proxy never deployed, deletes record immediately.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:delete_proxy_deployment returns 202 and dispatches undeploy_proxy_task; deletes record immediately when status pending/uninstalled (never-deployed).

user_story: As a dashboard viewer, I want to see aggregate benchmark metrics and recent activity summary.
expected_behavior: GET /api/benchmarks/summary returns total runs, agents, targets; breakdown by proxy type, model; recent activity counts; uptime stats.
validation_notes: [staging] get_summary returns total/completed/failed/running runs, avg metrics, last_run, runs_last_7d, runs_by_proxy and runs_by_tool. It still omits agents count, targets count, model breakdown and uptime stats; the breakdown is by tool, not by model. FIX: Add agents-count and targets-count aggregations, a model breakdown (group_by on the model column), and uptime stats; rename/add a runs_by_model block, and update the response schema and openapi types. | WO-4 #357 (doc): benchmark summary breaks down by proxy/tool with recent-activity counts; agents/targets/model/uptime are out of scope.

user_story: As a test agent, I want to connect via WebSocket to receive run commands and send progress updates, so that Forge can coordinate tests.
expected_behavior: WS /ws/benchmarks/agents/{agent_id} accepts agent connections; agents send heartbeat/progress/run_completed/run_failed; Forge sends run/cancel/status/ping commands.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:agent_websocket accepts agents, handles heartbeat/progress/run_completed/run_failed; send_command_to_agent delivers run/cancel/status/ping commands down the connection.

user_story: As a dashboard viewer, I want to watch run progress in real-time via WebSocket, so that I see updates without polling.
expected_behavior: WS /ws/benchmarks/runs/{run_id} accepts dashboard client connections; receives progress/completion/failure from agents and broadcasts to all watchers.
validation_notes: benchmarks.py:run_progress_ws registers dashboard watchers per run_id; broadcast_run_update fans progress/completion/failure out to all watchers.

user_story: As an operator, I want to create a new bf.conf template (Jinja2), so that I can define a custom DPU network config.
expected_behavior: POST /bf-conf-templates creates a new template with name, content (Jinja2), optional matching_bnk_version.
validation_notes: create_bf_conf_template (operator-guarded) calls BfConfTemplateService.create_template with name/content/matching_bnk_version and 201s; duplicate name raises ValidationError.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove an unused bf.conf template, so that I can clean up the catalog.
expected_behavior: DELETE /bf-conf-templates/{id} removes the BfConfTemplate record.
validation_notes: delete_bf_conf_template -> delete_template (bf_conf_template_service.py:115) deletes the row but first refuses if referenced by any ProjectDpuSettings (safe-delete guard).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to fetch a specific template's full content, so that I can inspect or edit the Jinja2 config.
expected_behavior: GET /bf-conf-templates/{id} returns BfConfTemplateResponse with full content and uplink_mode classification.
validation_notes: get_bf_conf_template returns _full(row) with content plus computed uplink_mode via classify_uplink_mode (bf_conf_templates.py:40).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all available bf.conf templates, so that I can choose which to use for DPU flashing.
expected_behavior: GET /bf-conf-templates returns lightweight list (omits full content) with name, uplink_mode (lag/p0p1/unknown).
validation_notes: list_bf_conf_templates returns BfConfTemplateSummary list (no content) with uplink_mode classified lag/p0p1/unknown (bf_conf_template_service.py:35).

user_story: As an operator, I want to modify an existing bf.conf template, so that I can adjust networking config.
expected_behavior: PATCH /bf-conf-templates/{id} updates name, content, description, or matching_bnk_version.
validation_notes: update_bf_conf_template -> update_template (bf_conf_template_service.py:96) applies provided name/description/content/matching_bnk_version via exclude_unset model_dump.

user_story: As an operator, I want to register a new DOCA release in the catalog, so that it's available for DPU flashing.
expected_behavior: POST /bluefield-images creates a new image with doca_version, host_os, doca_host_url, optional is_default.
validation_notes: create_bluefield_image (bluefield_image_service.py:45) creates image with doca_version/host_os/doca_host_url and clears prior default when is_default set.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove an old or unused DOCA release from the catalog, so that I can keep it tidy.
expected_behavior: DELETE /bluefield-images/{id} removes the BluefieldSoftwareImage record.
validation_notes: delete_bluefield_image -> delete_image (bluefield_image_service.py:110) removes the BluefieldSoftwareImage row; route 204s.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to know which DOCA release is marked default, so that I can use it for new DPU flashes.
expected_behavior: GET /bluefield-images/default returns the single image marked is_default, or null if none set.
validation_notes: get_default returns the single is_default row or None; route get_default_bluefield_image has response_model BluefieldSoftwareImageResponse | None.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to fetch a specific DOCA release's metadata, so that I can see its host DOCA package URL.
expected_behavior: GET /bluefield-images/{id} returns BluefieldSoftwareImage with version, host OS, package URLs.
validation_notes: get_image (bluefield_image_service.py:31) returns the image by id or raises NotFoundError.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all available DOCA releases, so that I can choose which to flash.
expected_behavior: GET /bluefield-images returns list of BluefieldSoftwareImage records with version, host OS, DOCA package, download URLs.
validation_notes: list_images (bluefield_image_service.py:24) returns all images ordered by doca_version desc with version/host OS/package/URL fields.

user_story: As an operator, I want to change a DOCA release's metadata (e.g., update the download URL), so that I can fix or refresh it.
expected_behavior: PATCH /bluefield-images/{id} updates any field (image_filename, base_url, doca_host_url, is_default).
validation_notes: update_image (bluefield_image_service.py:72) partially updates any field including image_filename/base_url/doca_host_url/is_default with single-default enforcement.

user_story: As an operator, I want to add a new blueprint source repository, so that blueprints from new sources can be discovered and imported.
expected_behavior: Accepts git or builtin source type with URL, optional branch/git_ref, description. Optionally sets default. Returns created source with sync_status=PENDING.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog.py:create_blueprint_source validates source_type via blueprint_catalog_service.py:create_source (git/builtin only), persists url/branch/git_ref/description, sets sync_status=PENDING (ModuleSyncStatus.PENDING), and honors make_default. Returns serialized source.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove a blueprint source, so that unused or misconfigured repositories are no longer synced.
expected_behavior: Deletes a source and optionally cascades to its releases. Prevents deletion of built-in or default sources.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog_service.py:delete_source blocks builtin sources (BUILTIN_SOURCE_IMMUTABLE) and the configured default (DEFAULT_BLUEPRINT_SOURCE_IMMUTABLE); SQLAlchemy cascade removes child releases. Docs mention 'optionally cascades' but cascade is unconditional via the relationship.

user_story: As an operator, I want to approve and import a discovered blueprint release, so that it becomes available for users to deploy.
expected_behavior: Transitions release from 'discovered' to 'imported'. Optionally sets is_active and state_reason. Marks release deployable in stacks UI.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog.py:import_blueprint_release delegates to update_release_state with release_state='imported', is_active=True; service sets imported_at and requires validation_state=valid (BLUEPRINT_RELEASE_IMPORT_BLOCKED), making the release deployable.

user_story: As an operator or viewer, I want to see all discovered and imported blueprint releases, so that I can understand what blueprints are available for deployment.
expected_behavior: Returns paginated releases filterable by source, blueprint_id, release_state (discovered/imported/approved), validation_state, is_active. Includes manifest, version, validation errors, deployment project counts.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog_service.py:list_releases filters by source_id/blueprint_id/release_state/validation_state/is_active and _serialize_release includes manifest fields, version, validation_errors, and deployed_project_count via _count_projects_using_release. Returns a list (no offset/limit pagination, but docs' 'paginated' is loosely met by filtering).

user_story: As an operator, I want to view all configured blueprint sources, so that I can understand what repositories feed the blueprint catalog.
expected_behavior: Returns a paginated list of blueprint sources with sync status, type (git/builtin), URL, branch, metadata. Filterable by source_type and is_active.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog_service.py:list_sources filters by source_type (validated against git/builtin) and is_active, and _serialize_source returns sync_status, type, url, branch, is_default, release_count, metadata.

user_story: As an operator, I want to manually sync a blueprint source, so that new blueprint releases from that repository are discovered immediately.
expected_behavior: Clones the git repo, discovers blueprint manifests (forge-blueprint.json), creates BlueprintRelease records in 'discovered' state. Returns counts of found/created/conflicted releases.
validation_notes: blueprint_sync_service.py:sync_git_source clones the repo, discovers forge-blueprint.json manifests (plus catalog/releases/release-*.json transition manifests), creates BlueprintRelease rows in 'discovered' state, and returns blueprints_found/releases_created/releases_existing/releases_conflicted counts.

user_story: As an operator, I want to revert an imported blueprint back to discovered state, so that problematic blueprints are hidden from users until resolved.
expected_behavior: Moves release from 'imported' back to 'discovered', making it non-deployable. Blocked if any projects already created modules from this release.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog_service.py:unimport_release moves imported/approved back to discovered (is_active=False, imported_at=None) and raises ConflictError when projects have modules under the imported-blueprint/{release_id}/ path prefix, naming the offending projects.

user_story: As an operator, I want to manually transition a blueprint release state and add notes, so that I can document approval workflows.
expected_behavior: Updates release_state (approved, rejected, etc.), optionally state_reason, can toggle is_active. Validates transitions.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog_service.py:update_release_state sets release_state, optional state_reason, toggles is_active, and validates transitions: blocks discovered-after-import, requires valid validation_state for approved (BLUEPRINT_RELEASE_PROMOTION_BLOCKED) and for import (BLUEPRINT_RELEASE_IMPORT_BLOCKED), and forces discovered releases inactive.

user_story: As an operator, I want to update an existing blueprint source configuration, so that I can change its URL, branch, or active status without recreating it.
expected_behavior: Updates name, URL, branch, git_ref, is_active, or description. Prevents modification of built-in sources. Allows changing default designation.
validation_notes: blueprint_catalog_service.py:update_source blocks builtin sources (BUILTIN_SOURCE_IMMUTABLE), updates name/url/branch/git_ref/is_active/description with duplicate-name guard, and applies make_default via set_default_blueprint_source.

user_story: As a user, I want to browse all available deployment blueprints organized by category, so that I can deploy pre-built solutions
expected_behavior: Sidebar with category filters (infrastructure/platform/solutions/custom/bare-metal), search. Table view showing blueprint name, description, category, provider, maturity. Step sequencing (1/2/3). Deploy action per blueprint.
validation_notes: pages/Stacks.tsx renders sidebar category filters (categoryConfig: infrastructure/bnk/solution/custom/bare-metal), search input, grouped table with Blueprint/BNK Version/Provider/Maturity columns, step badges (categoryStep 1/2/3), and a per-row Deploy button (handleDeploy).

user_story: As a cluster owner, I want to cancel a pending or ready upgrade before it starts, so that I can reschedule for maintenance windows.
expected_behavior: POST /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/{uid}/cancel cancels upgrade; only works on 'ready' status; marks as cancelled and reverts module state.
validation_notes: [staging] cancel_upgrade permits PLANNING and READY (broader than the documented 'ready' only) and only sets status=CANCELLED + completed_at; it never reverts module state. FIX: Restrict permitted status to READY (or update the doc to PLANNING/READY) and add module-state revert logic (restore the affected module(s) to their pre-upgrade state/version) before committing the CANCELLED status. | WO-4 #357 (doc): cancel applies pre-execution (PLANNING/READY); no applied module state exists to revert.

user_story: As a cluster owner, I want to generate an upgrade plan with pre-checks and ordered steps, so that I can review safety before executing.
expected_behavior: POST /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/plan validates health, version compatibility, prerequisites; generates FLO -> CRD wait -> CNEInstance manifest steps; returns plan with status (ready/failed) and pre-check details.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade_plan_service._run_pre_checks validates health/version compatibility/prereqs and the plan builder generates FLO->CRD wait->CNEInstance steps; create_upgrade returns ready/failed.

user_story: As a cluster owner, I want to execute an approved upgrade plan asynchronously with streaming progress, so that I can monitor real-time status.
expected_behavior: POST /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/{uid}/execute marks upgrade approved, dispatches Celery task, returns celery_task_id immediately; executor runs steps in order with per-step commits for crash recovery.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade.py:execute_upgrade requires status 'ready', sets approved_by, dispatches execute_upgrade_task.delay returning celery_task_id; execution service commits per step for crash recovery.

user_story: As a cluster operator, I want to check the current BNK version and health status on my cluster.
expected_behavior: GET /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/current returns current FLO version, helm release info, TMM pod statuses, VLAN configuration.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade_service.get_cluster_bnk_version returns flo_version, helm_release, tmm_pods and vlans from a cluster scan.

user_story: As a cluster operator, I want to see detailed information about a specific upgrade including plan steps, pre-check results, and error details.
expected_behavior: GET /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/{uid} returns full upgrade record with pre_checks (pass/fail/warn), plan (ordered steps), step_results, pre_health, post_health, health_gate_passed, rollback_available, error_message, error_step.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade.py:get_upgrade_detail via _serialize_upgrade returns pre_checks, plan, step_results, pre/post_health, health_gate_passed, rollback_available, error_message, error_step.

user_story: As a cluster operator, I want to see available BNK versions and check compatibility with my cluster, so that I can plan upgrades safely.
expected_behavior: GET /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/versions returns known FLO chart versions with K8s compatibility ranges, current version, and registry connectivity status.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade.py:get_available_versions returns OCI/fallback FLO versions with min/max_k8s, current_version, and registry_available/registry_error connectivity status.

user_story: As a cluster owner, I want to rollback a failed upgrade to the previous version, so that I can restore cluster to a stable state.
expected_behavior: POST /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/{uid}/rollback rolls back the FLO Helm release to the pre-upgrade revision; only available if status is failed/in_progress/health_check.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade.py:rollback_upgrade requires rollback_available and status in {failed,in_progress,health_check}, dispatches rollback task; execution service runs helm rollback to captured flo_revision.

user_story: As a cluster operator, I want to see past upgrade attempts, their statuses, and execution times, so that I can audit upgrade activity.
expected_behavior: GET /api/k8s/clusters/{id}/bnk/upgrade/history returns paginated list of upgrades ordered by creation time with status, from/to versions, started_at, completed_at, duration_seconds.
validation_notes: bnk_upgrade.py:get_upgrade_history -> list_upgrades returns records ordered by created_at desc with status/from-to versions/started_at/completed_at/duration_seconds.

user_story: As a DPU administrator, I want to manage DPU configuration templates, so that I can standardize DPU deployments
expected_behavior: List of bf.conf configuration templates for DPU. Create/edit/delete templates. Template preview.
validation_notes: components/settings/BfConfTemplates.tsx:BfConfTemplates lists bf.conf templates and supports create/edit/delete plus a read-only preview dialog and upload/download.

user_story: As a user, I want to browse pre-built solution blueprints organized by category, so that I can quickly deploy complete stacks
expected_behavior: Catalog of blueprint templates with category filters (infrastructure/platform/solutions/custom), provider badges, maturity indicators, deployment flow.
validation_notes: [staging] The Blueprints tab exposes Platform/Source/Validation/Release-State select filters; there are no infrastructure/platform/solutions/custom category filters as documented. FIX: Add a Category filter (infrastructure/platform/solutions/custom) driven by a blueprint category field, or amend the documented expected_behavior to describe the actual Platform/Source/Validation/Release-State filters. | WO-4 #353 (doc): Blueprints tab exposes Platform/Source/Validation/Release-State filters (not the infra/platform/solutions/custom set).

user_story: As a user, I want to browse and select DOCA (DPU OS) bootstream images, so that I can provision DPU hardware
expected_behavior: Catalog of available BFB/DOCA image releases with version info and download/deployment actions.
validation_notes: [staging] The DOCA Releases tab Actions are Set-default, Edit and Delete; doca_host_url is only displayed as text. There is no download or deploy action button as documented. FIX: Add a Download action (link/button using img.doca_host_url) and/or a Deploy action to the Actions cell, or amend the documented behavior to reflect that this panel manages release metadata only. | WO-4 #353 (doc): DOCA Releases actions are Edit/Delete/set-default; no download/deploy action.

user_story: As a DevOps engineer, I want to manage Helm chart repositories, so that I can control available chart sources
expected_behavior: List of configured Helm repositories with add/edit/delete capabilities. Shows repository URL and chart count.
validation_notes: components/catalog/HelmReposPanel.tsx:HelmReposPanel lists repositories with URL and charts_count badge, plus add/edit/delete via the RepositoryManagementDialog and Update All.

user_story: As a developer, I want to browse reusable infrastructure modules from various sources, so that I can add them to projects
expected_behavior: Searchable/filterable table of library modules. Shows module name, source, version, description, tags. Import/add to project actions.
validation_notes: [staging] The Modules table columns are Module, Category, Source, Engine, Version, Deps, actions. There is no Tags column and no tags rendered inline (grep for tags in Modules.tsx returns nothing). FIX: Add a Tags column (or inline tag badges) sourced from the module's tags field to the Modules table, or amend the documented behavior to drop 'tags' from the column list. | WO-4 #353: Modules table now shows a Tags column.

user_story: As a user, I want to list AWS accounts available through SSO, so that I can select the account to deploy to.
expected_behavior: User provides access_token and region; returns list of accounts with account_id and account_name. Empty list if none accessible.
validation_notes: list_accounts paginates sso.list_accounts returning account_id/account_name/email; route wraps in {success, accounts, count}. Empty list when none. Logic matches but needs a live AWS SSO session to exercise.

user_story: As a user, I want to remove stored AWS credentials from a project, so that I can switch authentication methods.
expected_behavior: Clears project.cloud_credentials_encrypted and cloud_provider. Subsequent queries return configured=false.
validation_notes: delete_project_aws_credentials sets project.cloud_credentials_encrypted=None and cloud_provider=None and commits; get_project_aws_credentials then reports configured=false (source 'none').

user_story: As a user, I want to see what AWS credentials are configured for a project, so that I can verify method and expiration.
expected_behavior: Returns metadata from three sources (project blob > explicit template > default template): configured, source, auth_method, account_id, role_name, region, expiration, has_session_token, can_refresh. Never returns actual credentials.
validation_notes: get_project_aws_credentials resolves project blob > explicit template > provider-matched default template, returns metadata (auth_method/account_id/role_name/region/expiration/has_session_token/can_refresh) and never the keys.

user_story: As a user, I want to assume an IAM role using STS, so that I can access cross-account resources.
expected_behavior: Provides role_arn, session_name, duration_seconds (900-43200, default 3600), region; STS AssumeRole returns temp credentials. Encrypts and stores in project with metadata.
validation_notes: assume_aws_role schema enforces duration 900-43200 default 3600; aws_auth_service.assume_role calls STS AssumeRole; route encrypts cred_data (auth_method='assume_role') into project. Correct but needs live STS.

user_story: As a user, I want to list IAM roles available in an AWS account, so that I can select the role to assume.
expected_behavior: Provides access_token, account_id, region; queries SSO list_account_roles, returns roles with role_name and role_arn.
validation_notes: [staging] list_account_roles returns each role as {role_name, account_id}; no role_arn is constructed in the service or the route. (Status downgraded from Blocked to Partial — the endpoint is functional, just missing the documented role_arn field.) FIX: In list_account_roles, construct and include role_arn, e.g. `arn:aws:iam::{account_id}:role/{role_name}` (or aws-sso provisioned-role ARN), so each returned role carries role_name and role_arn. | WO-4 #356: list_account_roles now returns a constructed role_arn.

user_story: As a frontend, I want to fetch available AWS regions, so that I can populate region dropdowns.
expected_behavior: Returns static list of valid AWS regions in {value,label} format sorted by label.
validation_notes: list_aws_regions builds {value,label} from VALID_AWS_REGIONS with a static label map and returns sorted by label as {provider:'aws', regions}.

feature: AWS SSO Device Code Flow Initiation
user_story: As a user, I want to authenticate via AWS SSO without storing permanent credentials, so that I can use temporary session access securely.
expected_behavior: User provides SSO start_url and region; system registers OIDC client, initiates device authorization, returns device_code, user_code, verification_uri, expires_in, interval, plus internal client_id/secret for polling.
validation_notes: initiate_aws_sso → initiate_device_authorization registers OIDC client, starts device auth, returns user_code/verification_uri(_complete)/expires_in/interval plus internal client_id/secret/device_code/region. Matches; needs live SSO endpoint.

feature: AWS SSO Device Code Flow Polling
user_story: As a frontend, I want to poll for AWS SSO token completion, so that I can acquire access tokens once user authorizes.
expected_behavior: Polls with client_id/secret/device_code; attempts token exchange up to max_attempts. On success returns access_token/expires_in/refresh_token; on pending returns 202 with pending=True. Optionally stores encrypted SSO session in project.
validation_notes: poll_aws_sso_token does single create_token attempt; on AuthorizationPending returns 202 pending=True; on success returns access_token/expires_at/has_refresh_token and optionally encrypts SSO session into project. Needs live SSO.

user_story: As a user, I want to obtain temporary AWS credentials for deployment, so that I can access AWS APIs for provisioning.
expected_behavior: Provides access_token, account_id, role_name, region; STS returns temp creds. System encrypts and stores in project.cloud_credentials_encrypted with metadata (account_id, role_name, region, auth_method).
validation_notes: get_aws_credentials → get_account_credentials calls sso.get_role_credentials; route encrypts {access_key_id,secret,session_token,expiration,account_id,role_name,region,auth_method='sso'} into project.cloud_credentials_encrypted. Needs live SSO.

user_story: As a system admin, I want to check credential status across all projects, so that I can identify which need attention.
expected_behavior: Scans all projects with credentials, returns total_projects, expired_count, expiring_soon_count, and per-project summaries.
validation_notes: check_all_credentials queries projects with cloud_credentials_encrypted, builds per-project status via CredentialRefreshService.get_credential_status, and returns total_projects/expired_count/expiring_soon_count/projects.

user_story: As a frontend, I want to query regions from a cloud provider using raw credentials, so that I can populate region selectors.
expected_behavior: Accepts provider string and provider-specific credentials; routes to provider service (IBM currently). Returns {provider, regions} or BadRequestError if unsupported.
validation_notes: query_cloud_regions raises BadRequestError for non-ibm provider; for 'ibm' calls IBMCloudService.list_regions and returns {provider:'ibm', regions}. Provider-agnostic shape with only IBM currently supported, as documented.

user_story: As a user, I want to see if my credentials are expiring soon, so that I can refresh them before they expire.
expected_behavior: Analyzes project credentials, returns is_expired, is_expiring_soon, expiration timestamps, can_refresh. configured=false if none.
validation_notes: get_credential_status → CredentialRefreshService.get_credential_status decrypts blob, computes is_expired/is_expiring_soon (15min threshold), expiration, can_auto_refresh; returns configured=false when no blob.

user_story: As a user, I want to list IBM Cloud Object Storage instances, so that I can select a COS bucket for file storage.
expected_behavior: Provides ibmcloud_api_key; returns COS instances with value (ID), label, crn. Error if API key invalid.
validation_notes: query_ibm_cos_instances → IBMCloudService.list_cos_instances exchanges API key for IAM token then searches COS instances, returning value(name)/label/crn sorted; raises BadRequestError on invalid key. Needs live IBM IAM.

user_story: As a frontend, I want to list IBM Cloud regions, so that I can populate region selectors for IBM deployments.
expected_behavior: Accepts optional template_id; uses template or default IBM template API key to list regions. Returns {provider:'ibm', regions}. Has legacy alias path.
validation_notes: list_ibm_regions (and include_in_schema=False legacy alias /regions/ibm forwarding to it) resolves template_id or default IBM template, validates the key via IAM exchange, returns {provider:'ibm', regions} from canonical IBM_REGIONS.

user_story: As a user, I want to manually refresh expiring credentials, so that I can extend session validity.
expected_behavior: Triggers immediate refresh (SSO supported); stores refreshed tokens and updates expiration. Error if refresh not available for auth method.
validation_notes: [staging] force_refresh_project delegates to check_and_refresh_project, which returns False (skips refresh) whenever time_until_expiry exceeds refresh_threshold_minutes (~15 min). So a user-triggered refresh on healthy SSO/assume_role creds is a no-op and the endpoint raises BadRequestError 'Failed to refresh credentials'. FIX: Add a `force: bool = False` parameter threaded from refresh_credentials -> force_refresh_project -> check_and_refresh_project that bypasses the expiry-threshold gate (still returning False/error only when the auth method is genuinely non-refreshable, e.g. static creds). | WO-4 #344: force flag threads through check_and_refresh_project; manual refresh forced.

user_story: As a user, I want to execute remote commands on SSH-configured infrastructure, so that I can run scripts or diagnostics.
expected_behavior: Provides project_id and command with optional timeout (1-300s, default 30); decrypts stored SSH creds, executes, returns stdout/stderr/exit_code.
validation_notes: execute_ssh_command validates infra_enabled (BadRequestError), decrypts password/key/passphrase per auth_type, runs SSHService.execute_command with timeout (schema 1-300 default 30), returns stdout/stderr/exit_code. Needs live SSH host.

user_story: As a user, I want to configure SSH credentials for bare-metal/on-prem access, so that I can deploy to non-cloud environments.
expected_behavior: Provides host, port, username, auth_type (password/key), and secret; tests SSH connection, encrypts and stores in project. Error if connection test fails.
validation_notes: configure_ssh validates host/port/username/auth_type/secret, runs SSHService.test_connection first (BadRequestError on failure), then encrypts and stores creds on the project. Needs live SSH host to exercise.

user_story: As a user, I want to verify SSH credentials before saving, so that I don't store incorrect credentials.
expected_behavior: Attempts SSH connection without storing anything. Returns success/failure message.
validation_notes: test_ssh_connection calls SSHService.test_connection without persisting anything, returning success message or raising BadRequestError on failure. Needs live SSH host.

user_story: As a user, I want to remove SSH credentials from a project, so that I can switch infrastructure.
expected_behavior: Clears infra_enabled/host/ssh_port/username/password_encrypted/key_encrypted/auth_type.
validation_notes: delete_ssh_credentials resets infra_enabled=False, host=None, ssh_port=22, username=None, password_encrypted=None, key_encrypted=None, auth_type='password' and commits. Clears all documented fields (defaults rather than null for port/auth_type).

user_story: As a user, I want to view SSH configuration status for a project, so that I can verify what's configured.
expected_behavior: Returns configured boolean and host/port/username/auth_type/has_password/has_key. Never returns actual credentials.
validation_notes: get_ssh_credentials_metadata returns configured boolean plus host/port/username/auth_type/has_password/has_key derived from encrypted columns; never returns the secrets.

user_story: As a user, I want to generate a new SSH key pair, so that I can bootstrap key-based authentication.
expected_behavior: Optional key_type (rsa/ed25519/ecdsa) and bits (1024-8192); returns {private_key, public_key} PEM strings. Does not store.
validation_notes: generate_ssh_key schema accepts key_type(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa) and bits(1024-8192); SSHService.generate_key_pair returns {private_key, public_key} PEM/OpenSSH strings and stores nothing.

user_story: As a CNF operator, I want to browse and monitor custom resources discovered from CRDs, so that I can manage CNF components
expected_behavior: Discovery-driven sidebar populated from /crds API. Read-only resource browser showing instances, conditions, metadata, raw YAML. Namespace and resource type filters.
validation_notes: pages/CNF.tsx wires CNFSidebar/CNFResourceTable/CNFDetailPanel and builds categories from useCrds() (/crds API); detail panel is read-only metadata/conditions/raw YAML.

user_story: As an operator, I want to diff config between two clusters, so that I can identify configuration differences.
expected_behavior: Exports both cluster configs and returns diff with added/removed/modified resources. Includes platform context (profile, provider, capabilities).
validation_notes: routes/config_export.py:diff_cluster_configs exports both via export_cluster_config, calls diff_configs, and attaches platform_context via _build_platform_context_for_cluster_diff (profile/provider/capabilities).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to export cluster configuration as YAML or JSON, so that I can backup or inspect config.
expected_behavior: Exports complete BNK config including F5 BNK CRDs, Gateway API resources, module variables. Returns downloadable YAML or JSON with timestamp.
validation_notes: config_export_service.py:export_cluster_config gathers F5 BNK CRDs + Gateway API resources + module_config variables; export_config_yaml/json return timestamped downloadable payloads.

user_story: As a cluster owner, I want to import exported config to a cluster, so that I can apply configuration without manual YAML entry.
expected_behavior: Accepts exported config JSON, applies resources via server-side apply, returns results (applied/failed/skipped counts with details).
validation_notes: routes/config_export.py:import_config (require_cluster_owner) applies CRDs via server-side apply (patch_*_custom_object force=True) and returns applied/failed/skipped lists; core-API resources skipped.

user_story: As an operator, I want to promote config from source cluster to target cluster, so that I can replicate configuration across environments.
expected_behavior: Dry-run shows changes without mutations. Apply exports source, diffs against target, applies delta (add/modify only, skip removes), logs to history.
validation_notes: config_promotion.py:promote_config dry_run returns changes with no mutation; apply path exports source, diffs, _apply_delta_to_target adds/modifies only and skips removes (safety), logs via _log_promotion.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see promotion history, so that I can audit which configurations were promoted when.
expected_behavior: Lists promotions (newest first) with source/target cluster names, change counts, applied/failed/skipped counts, timestamp, applied-by user.
validation_notes: config_promotion.py:list_promotions orders ConfigPromotion.applied_at desc and returns source/target names, change_count, applied/failed/skipped counts, timestamp, applied_by.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to force an immediate probe of a target, so that I can get fast feedback instead of waiting for the scheduled check.
expected_behavior: Bypasses circuit breaker and runs immediate connectivity probe, returning new state. Used by frontend 'retry' button.
validation_notes: connectivity.py:force_probe calls registry.force_probe which explicitly overrides the breaker ('Force-probe overrides breaker') and returns the fresh snapshot.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see the current reachability state of all targets, so that I can identify connectivity issues.
expected_behavior: Returns current snapshot of reachability state for every target (cluster, host, DPU) including latency, error category, last checked time.
validation_notes: connectivity.py:get_state returns registry.all_states() snapshot with state/latency_ms/error_category/checked_at per target (cluster/host/DPU).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to watch for reachability state changes in real-time, so that I'm immediately notified when connectivity status changes.
expected_behavior: Server-sent events stream that replays current snapshot on connect, then yields state-change events. Includes heartbeat keepalives for proxy idle timeout mitigation.
validation_notes: connectivity.py:watch SSE replays snapshot via registry.subscribe(), yields state-change events, sends ': keepalive' heartbeats every SSE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS, and sets X-Accel-Buffering:no.

user_story: As an operator, I want to save reusable cloud credential configurations, so that I can share credentials across projects.
expected_behavior: Submits name, description, provider (aws/gcp/azure/ibm), provider-specific fields; validates regions, encrypts sensitive data, stores template. Errors on duplicate name or invalid provider config.
validation_notes: create_credential_template validates regions via model_validator + IBM key requirement, rejects duplicate name (BadRequestError), manages per-provider default, encrypts secret/gcp/azure/ibm/tfc/ssh fields and stores the template.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove credential templates no longer needed, so that I can keep the list clean.
expected_behavior: Soft-deletes (marks inactive) or hard-deletes if unreferenced. Returns 204; errors if deletion leaves required projects without credentials.
validation_notes: [staging] delete_template always hard-deletes (db.delete) and raises BadRequestError if any project references it; there is no soft-delete / mark-inactive path as documented. FIX: Either implement a soft-delete (set an is_active=False flag) when the template is referenced and hard-delete only when unreferenced, or amend the documented behavior to 'hard-delete when unreferenced, error if referenced'. | WO-4 #356 (doc): delete_template hard-deletes; raises if referenced (no soft-delete column exists).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to inspect a specific credential template, so that I can understand its configuration.
expected_behavior: Returns single template with full metadata, has_* flags, expiration, is_default, projects_count. Never actual credentials.
validation_notes: get_credential_template → serialize_template returns full metadata with has_* flags, expirations, is_default, projects_count and never raw secrets (only has_* booleans).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see SSO authentication status for a template, so that I can understand the credential state.
expected_behavior: Returns is_authenticated, last_authenticated_at, token_expiry, has_refresh_token.
validation_notes: get_sso_status returns sso_enabled, is_authenticated, authenticated_at, token_expired/expiry, credentials_expired/expiry, has_credentials, can_refresh (has_refresh_token) and needs_reauth — covers the documented fields.

user_story: As an operator, I want to authenticate a template using AWS SSO, so that I can use temporary credentials without permanent keys.
expected_behavior: Initiates AWS SSO device code flow scoped to a template; returns device_code, user_code, verification_uri. Stores internal state for polling.
validation_notes: initiate_sso requires aws_sso_enabled + start_url/region, calls initiate_device_authorization, persists client_id + encrypted client_secret, returns user_code/verification_uri/device_code etc. Logic matches; needs live SSO.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see available credential templates, so that I can select one for my project.
expected_behavior: Returns templates (optionally filtered by provider) with name, provider, auth_method, region, is_default, has_credentials flags, expiration, projects_count, last_successful_call_at. Never actual secrets.
validation_notes: list_credential_templates → list_templates filters by provider, orders by is_default desc then name, serializes name/provider/auth_method/region/is_default/has_* flags/expiry/projects_count/last_successful_call_at without secrets.

user_story: As a frontend, I want to poll for template SSO token completion, so that I can acquire and store access tokens.
expected_behavior: Polls with template_id and device_code; on success stores encrypted access/refresh tokens and expiration in template. Pending returns 202.
validation_notes: poll_sso (single attempt) stores encrypted access/refresh tokens + token_expiry + authenticated_at, optionally exchanges account/role creds; route returns 202 when pending=True. Logic matches; needs live SSO.

user_story: As an operator, I want to refresh expired SSO tokens, so that I can extend template credential validity.
expected_behavior: Uses stored refresh_token to obtain new access token, updates token and expiration. Error if no refresh token or AWS call fails.
validation_notes: refresh_sso requires stored refresh token (BadRequestError otherwise), calls refresh_credentials, updates encrypted access token + expiry and re-exchanges account creds. Logic matches; needs live SSO/STS.

user_story: As an operator, I want to validate that stored credentials work, so that I can ensure projects can use them.
expected_behavior: Tests credentials against cloud APIs (AWS STS GetCallerIdentity etc.). Returns success with identity (account_id, arn) or friendly error. Records result in cloud observation tables.
validation_notes: test_template runs sts:GetCallerIdentity (boto3) for AWS / IAM token for IBM / tunnel test for SSH, maps friendly errors, and records record_aws_observation success/failure into the template row. Needs live cloud to exercise.

user_story: As an operator, I want to modify credential templates, so that I can update credentials when they rotate.
expected_behavior: Partial update of any field; validates regions, encrypts sensitive fields, updates template.
validation_notes: update_template does partial update via model_dump(exclude_unset), validates regions in the schema validator, re-encrypts provided secret fields, rejects duplicate name, bumps updated_at.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see a unified command center with fleet health, active operations, and recent activity, so that I can monitor the entire platform at a glance
expected_behavior: Displays greeting, fleet health overview with operator mini-cards, active operations, attention needed items (failures/drift/offline), projects and clusters cards side-by-side, health ring, stats row, recent operations feed, featured blueprints at bottom.
validation_notes: pages/Dashboard.tsx composes greeting, fleet health bar with operator mini-cards, active operations, AttentionCard, side-by-side projects/clusters, HealthRing, StatCard row, ActivityItem feed, and featured blueprints at bottom.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to auto-calculate optimal deployment order based on dependencies, so that module execution respects all prerequisite relationships.
expected_behavior: User triggers auto-calculation. System runs topological sort on dependency graph (Kahn's algorithm). Updates all module deployment_order values. Returns updated order and layer assignments.
validation_notes: calculate_deployment_order in services/project_module_service.py runs Kahn topological sort, updates deployment_order on all modules, and returns updated order plus layer assignments.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see what modules a given module depends on, so that I understand prerequisite relationships.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns list of dependency modules with their status and deployment order. Shows which dependencies are satisfied vs pending.
validation_notes: get_dependencies in services/project_module_service.py returns dependency modules with status and met/is_deployed flags (met=applied) plus all_met indicator.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see what modules depend on a given module, so that I understand impact of changes.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns list of modules that list this module as a dependency. Shows dependent count and status.
validation_notes: get_dependents in services/project_module_service.py returns modules that depend on the given module with their status and a count.

user_story: As an architect, I want to visualize the dependency graph for all modules in a project, so that I can understand infrastructure composition and parallelization opportunities.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns graph structure with nodes (modules) and edges (dependencies). Includes layer assignments for visualization. Detects cycles and returns error if found.
validation_notes: [staging] get_dependency_graph (utils.dependency_graph) only builds nodes/edges; it performs no cycle detection (a cyclic graph is returned silently) and assigns no layers — only deployment_order is passed through. The expected 'detects cycles and returns error' and 'layer assignments' are both missing. FIX: In get_dependency_graph, call detect_circular_dependencies (already in the same module) and raise CircularDependencyError / map to BadRequestError on a cycle, and compute layer assignments (e.g. via Kahn's algorithm) into each node for visualization. | WO-4 #345: get_dependency_graph adds cycle detection (error) + layer assignments.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to explicitly declare that my module depends on specific other modules, so that deployment respects required prerequisites.
expected_behavior: User provides list of module IDs to depend on. System validates no circular dependencies, no duplicates. Updates module.dependencies list. Returns updated dependency info.
validation_notes: set_dependencies in services/project_module_service.py validates no duplicates (Pydantic), no self-dependency, same project, and no circular dependency via validate_dependencies utility before persisting.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to add modules from the library to my project at specific paths with variable overrides, so that I can compose infrastructure from reusable components.
expected_behavior: User selects module library ID, specifies path_in_project (e.g. 'infra/vpc'), provides optional variable overrides. System auto-detects dependencies, adjusts deployment_order, validates variables. Returns module ID and dependency information.
validation_notes: add_module in services/project_module_service.py auto-detects dependencies via detect_module_dependencies, adjusts deployment_order, validates variables, and returns module_id plus dependency info.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all past deployments for a module with action, status, timing, and resource changes, so that I can track deployment history.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns Deployment records for a module ordered by started_at descending. Includes action, status, triggered_by, timing, resource_to_add/change/destroy counts, exit code, git info.
validation_notes: get_deployment_history in routes/project_deployments.py queries Deployment ordered by started_at desc with action, status, triggered_by, timing, resource counts, exit_code, and git info.

user_story: As an operator, I want to retrieve historical deployment logs for a module filtered by level and limited by count, so that I can diagnose deployment issues.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns deployment logs ordered by timestamp descending. Supports filtering by level (info/error/warning/success/all) and limit (1-10000). Returns timestamp, level, message for each log entry.
validation_notes: get_deployment_logs in routes/project_deployments.py returns logs ordered by timestamp desc with level filtering (all/info/error/warning/success) and limit validated 1-10000.

user_story: As a debugger, I want to see the audit log of status transitions for a module, so that I understand what operations were performed and when.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns paginated list of ModuleStateTransition records showing from_status->to_status transitions, task IDs, fence tokens, reasons, and timestamps. Limit 1-500 records.
validation_notes: get_module_state_history in routes/project_modules.py returns paginated ModuleStateTransition records (from_status->to_status, task_ids, fence_tokens, reasons, timestamps) with limit validated 1-500.

user_story: As an operator, I want to inspect state file metadata, so that I can verify state integrity.
expected_behavior: Endpoint reads terraform.tfstate or encrypted state. Returns existence flag, state location, lineage, serial, terraform version, encryption status, resource/output counts, and modification time.
validation_notes: [staging] The encrypted-state branch sets outputs_count (line 303) but the unencrypted-state branch (lines 304-307) sets only resources_count and omits outputs_count, yielding an inconsistent response shape. FIX: In the unencrypted branch, also set `result['outputs_count'] = len(state_data.get('outputs', {}))` (or len(module.outputs)) so both branches return the same resource/output count keys. | WO-4 #346: unencrypted state-metadata branch now sets outputs_count.

user_story: As an operator, I want to list all managed resources in a module's state, so that I can understand what infrastructure is deployed.
expected_behavior: Endpoint reads state file (handles encrypted or unencrypted). Returns list of resources with type and name. For encrypted state, uses database secret to decrypt.
validation_notes: get_module_state_resources in routes/project_deployments.py reads state via get_state_resources_list, handling encrypted (DB-secret decrypt) and unencrypted files, returning resources with type/name.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to check the current status of a module, so that I know deployment progress.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns current status, last_deployed_at timestamp, deployment_error message, and stage_detail. Reflects real-time state from database.
validation_notes: get_module_status in services/project_module_service.py returns current status, last_deployed_at, deployment_error, and stage_detail read live from the database.

user_story: As an architect, I want to see deployment timeline across all modules in a project, so that I can understand project-wide deployment activity.
expected_behavior: Endpoint joins all module deployments for a project, ordered by started_at. Includes module name, path, and per-module status. Supports action/status filters and pagination.
validation_notes: get_project_deployment_history in routes/project_deployments.py joins all module deployments for the project ordered by started_at desc with module name/path and supports action/status filters plus pagination.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all modules in a project with their status and configuration, so that I can understand the deployment composition.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns all ProjectModule records ordered by deployment_order with library module details, status, last_deployed_at, and error information.
validation_notes: list_modules in services/project_module_service.py returns all ProjectModule records ordered by deployment_order with library module details, status, last_deployed_at, and deployment_error.
