user_story: As an operator, I want to recover a lost state file for a deployed module using outputs, so that I can regain management of infrastructure.
expected_behavior: User triggers state recovery on an applied module with outputs in database. System creates refresh task via Celery. Returns task ID and runs 'tofu refresh' to rebuild state from real infrastructure.
validation_notes: recover_state_file in routes/project_deployments.py verifies APPLIED status and DB outputs, creates a Task, and queues run_opentofu_refresh via Celery, returning the task_id.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to delete a module from a project, so that I can clean up unused infrastructure.
expected_behavior: System checks module lock (prevents deletion during active operation). Cleans up persistent workspace directory. Cascades deletion to state file and outputs. Returns success confirmation.
validation_notes: remove_module in services/project_module_service.py checks the module lock via ModuleLockService, cleans the persistent workspace via WorkspaceManager, and cascades deletion of state/outputs.

user_story: As an operator, I want to rematerialize infrastructure access details without a full redeploy, so that I can fix access metadata issues quickly.
expected_behavior: User calls repair on applied module. System normalizes module outputs in-place, fixing infrastructure_private_key_path and infrastructure_access_status. Returns repair status and key availability.
validation_notes: repair_infrastructure_access in routes/project_deployments.py calls normalize_module_outputs_in_place on applied modules and returns repair status with key availability/access metadata.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to modify variable overrides, deployment order, or enabled status, so that I can adjust module behavior without removing it.
expected_behavior: User updates one or more of: variable_overrides (validates against schema), deployment_order, or enabled flag. System validates variables and persists changes. Returns updated module metadata.
validation_notes: update_module in services/project_module_service.py validates variable_overrides against schema and updates deployment_order/enabled, returning updated metadata and optional warnings.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to register discovered DPU-host nodes as bare-metal hosts, so that I can manage physical infrastructure.
expected_behavior: Creates bare-metal host record from discovered node with optional custom naming. Idempotent — reregistering existing hosts returns existing record with status='exists'.
validation_notes: discovery.py:register_node_as_host / register_all_hosts delegate to discovery_service.register_node_as_bare_metal_host; idempotent re-register returns existing row with status='exists'.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to list, view, rerun, and delete discovery jobs, so that I can manage discovery workflows.
expected_behavior: Lists jobs with status/progress, gets job details with discovered nodes, reruns completed/failed jobs, deletes jobs with cleanup.
validation_notes: discovery.py list/get/rerun/delete endpoints delegate to DiscoveryService; rerun resets job to PENDING and re-executes, delete removes job + discovered nodes.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to register discovered DPU nodes in the DPU inventory, so that I can manage DPU infrastructure.
expected_behavior: Detects whether discovered IP is DPU BMC or DPU OS, creates DPU record with access_mode, BMC IP, optional host association.
validation_notes: discovery.py:register_node_as_dpu detects is_dpu_bmc vs is_dpu_node (400 if neither), sets access_mode/bmc_ip; discovery_service enforces duplicate-BMC guard and optional host association.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to probe kubeconfig contexts from a discovered node, so that I can register Kubernetes clusters that were discovered.
expected_behavior: SSHes to discovered node and retrieves kubeconfig contexts/clusters available on that node. Used in cluster auto-registration workflow.
validation_notes: discovery.py:probe_node_kubeconfig (require_project_owner) delegates to discovery_service.probe_node_kubeconfig which SSHes to the node and returns kubeconfig contexts/clusters.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to discover bare-metal hosts and DPUs via SSH, so that I can inventory infrastructure and register nodes.
expected_behavior: Triggers SSH discovery job against IP list with configurable credentials. Probes hardware (DPUs, NICs, BIOS), detects node types (BMC/DPU-OS/host), reports discovered nodes.
validation_notes: discovery.py:trigger_discovery accepts node/credential payload, creates job, and starts background SSH discovery via DiscoveryService.start_background_execution.

user_story: As an operator, I want to auto-assign VLAN IPs to all DPUs from project subnets, so that I can quickly populate IP addressing.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/auto-assign-vlan-ips assigns external/internal VLAN IPv4/IPv6 addresses sequentially from project subnets.
validation_notes: auto_assign_vlan_ips (dpu_service.py:273) assigns external/internal v4+v6 plus extras sequentially by DPU id using start_host+index from project subnets.

user_story: As an operator, I want to abort an in-flight flash, so that I can stop a failed upload.
expected_behavior: DELETE /dpus/{id}/flash revokes the Celery task with SIGTERM, sets flash_status to cancelled.
validation_notes: cancel_flash (dpus.py:708) revokes flash_celery_task_id with terminate=True signal=SIGTERM and sets flash_status=cancelled when uploading.

user_story: As an operator, I want to flip a DPU from InfiniBand to Ethernet mode and reboot, so that I can switch link modes.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/convert-to-ethernet validates IB mode, then enqueues task to run mlxconfig on both ports and reset.
validation_notes: convert_dpu_to_ethernet (dpus.py:318) does synchronous IB-mode preflight via _derive_link_mode then enqueues convert_to_ethernet_task; DpuLinkModeService runs mlxconfig LINK_TYPE=ETH + reset.

user_story: As an operator, I want to register a new DPU in the project, so that I can manage its configuration.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus creates a new DPU record with auto-assigned VLAN IPs from project subnets based on ordinal sequence.
validation_notes: create_dpu (dpu_service.py:108) derives ordinal=existing_count+1 and auto-populates external/internal VLAN v4/v6 from project subnets when caller omits them.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove a DPU record from the project, so that I can clean up deregistered hardware.
expected_behavior: DELETE /dpus/{id} removes the DPU record and cascades cleanup of related flash tasks.
validation_notes: delete_dpu (dpu_service.py:367) deletes the project-scoped DPU; related flash tasks cascade via DB FK (model-level ON DELETE).

user_story: As an operator, I want to stop and disable rshim on a DPU, so that I can free the serial console device.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/disable-rshim enqueues a task that stops rshim systemd unit and disables it persistently.
validation_notes: disable_rshim (dpus.py:267) marks running and enqueues disable_rshim_task which stops + persistently disables the rshim unit on the owning side.

user_story: As an operator, I want to probe all DPUs in a project at once, so that I can refresh the entire fleet's inventory.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/discover-all marks all DPUs as running and enqueues up to 10 parallel Redfish probes.
validation_notes: [staging] discover_all_dpus loops over every DPU and calls probe_dpu_task.delay once per DPU with no enqueue-time cap; MAX_PARALLEL_PROBES (10) is only echoed in the response and never gates enqueue. FIX: Enforce the cap at enqueue time — e.g. chunk/batch the DPUs into waves of MAX_PARALLEL_PROBES (or use a chord/group with a concurrency limit, or stamp tasks onto a queue whose worker concurrency is bounded), instead of unconditionally dispatching one task per DPU. | WO-4 #355: discover-all enqueues in waves of MAX_PARALLEL_PROBES (cap enforced).

user_story: As an operator, I want to probe a DPU's hardware inventory via Redfish, so that I can determine its current firmware and capabilities.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/discover enqueues an async Redfish probe capturing BIOS, BMC, NIC firmware versions, serial numbers, MAC addresses.
validation_notes: discover_dpu (dpus.py:163) enqueues probe_dpu_task; DpuDiscoveryService.run_and_persist runs the BlueField Redfish probe capturing inventory (BIOS/BMC/NIC fw, serials, MACs) onto the row.

user_story: As an operator, I want to test ping connectivity between all DPUs in a project, so that I can verify network topology.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/connectivity-matrix/run enqueues pairwise SSH+ping sweep; GET returns latest matrix with success/failure for each pair.
validation_notes: run_dpu_connectivity_matrix (dpus.py:68) marks running + enqueues the sweep and GET returns the persisted matrix; DpuConnectivityService.run does pairwise SSH+ping per source/target endpoint.

user_story: As an operator, I want to configure per-project DPU defaults, so that I can streamline repeated DPU operations.
expected_behavior: GET /dpu-settings returns project defaults (VLAN subnets, NTP/DNS servers, default credentials, template/image). PATCH updates.
validation_notes: get_dpu_settings (get_or_create) and update_dpu_settings (dpus.py:746) expose/patch ProjectDpuSettings defaults (subnets, NTP/DNS, creds, template/image).

user_story: As an operator, I want to persistently enable rshim on a BMC-mode DPU's BMC, so that /dev/rshim0 survives reboot.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/enable-rshim-on-bmc enqueues a task that SSHes to BMC and runs systemctl enable rshim.
validation_notes: enable_rshim_on_bmc (dpus.py:291) enqueues enable_rshim_on_bmc_task which SSHes to the BMC and runs systemctl enable+restart rshim.

user_story: As an operator, I want to reset a DPU to defaults (BIOS/BMC/NIC), so that I can clean it up for redeployment.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/reset-to-defaults runs layered Redfish resets (BIOS + BMC + NIC mlxconfig) based on selected options.
validation_notes: reset_dpu_to_defaults (dpus.py:491) builds FactoryResetOptions(bios/bmc/nic/bmc_deep) and DpuFactoryResetService.run performs layered Redfish BIOS+BMC + NIC mlxconfig resets.

user_story: As an operator, I want to flash all DPUs in a project, so that I can deploy a fleet at once.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/flash-all pre-validates each DPU's render (skipping broken configs), then enqueues parallel flash tasks.
validation_notes: flash_all_dpus (dpus.py:610) pre-renders each DPU (collecting render_failures to skip broken configs) then enqueues flash_dpu_task per renderable DPU.

user_story: As an operator, I want to flash a DPU with a BFB image and bf.conf, so that I can deploy a new DPU OS.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/flash renders bf.conf, downloads/caches BFB, opens SFTP to rshim, streams BFB+config, waits for reboot.
validation_notes: flash_dpu (dpus.py:571) does a synchronous render_only preflight (400 on failure) then enqueues flash_dpu_task; DpuFlashService renders bf.conf, caches BFB, SFTPs to rshim, awaits reboot.

user_story: As an operator, I want to view a specific DPU's configuration and discovery inventory, so that I can inspect its state.
expected_behavior: GET /dpus/{id} returns full DPU record including BMC credentials, VLAN config, discovery payload, flash status.
validation_notes: get_dpu -> DpuService.get_dpu returns DpuResponse with VLAN config, discovery payload pointers, flash status; BMC creds surface via presence/has flags + reveal endpoint, not plaintext.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see the last-captured hardware inventory for a DPU, so that I can inspect its discovered specs.
expected_behavior: GET /dpus/{id}/inventory returns the full Redfish discovery payload cached on the DPU row, or null if never probed.
validation_notes: get_dpu_inventory (dpus.py:142) returns last_discovery_payload (inventory) plus status/error/timestamp, null inventory when never probed.

user_story: As an operator, I want to download the last-rendered bf.conf, so that I can review or archive it.
expected_behavior: GET /dpus/{id}/rendered-bf-conf returns the persisted bf.conf content or 404 if never rendered.
validation_notes: get_rendered_dpu_bf_conf (dpus.py:686) returns last_rendered_bf_conf content or raises NotFoundError (404) when never rendered.

user_story: As an operator, I want to install rshim + MFT on a DPU's host, so that I can enable serial console access.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/install-rshim enqueues an async task that APT-installs rshim and mft, then chains a Discover probe.
validation_notes: install_rshim (dpus.py:239) marks running and enqueues install_rshim_task that apt-installs rshim+mft and chains a Discover probe on success.

user_story: As an operator, I want to list all DPUs in a project, so that I can see their inventory and status.
expected_behavior: GET /dpus returns all DPU records for the project with BMC IP, access mode, discovery status, flash status.
validation_notes: list_dpus -> DpuService.list_dpus returns all project DPUs with bmc_ip, access_mode, discovery status, and flash status via _to_response.

user_story: As an operator, I want to detect the DPU OS IP and verify SSH reachability, so that I can connect to the DPU Linux.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/probe-dpu-os enqueues task to probe via BMC (DHCP status) or SSH-verify to populate dpu_os_ip.
validation_notes: probe_dpu_os (dpus.py:522) marks probing and enqueues probe_dpu_os_task; DpuOsProbeService probes via BMC/SSH-verify and records dpu_os_ip on success.

feature: Probe DPU OS for all DPUs
user_story: As an operator, I want to probe the OS on all DPUs at once, so that I can bulk-populate OS IP addresses.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/probe-dpu-os-all enqueues probes for every DPU in the project (up to 10 parallel).
validation_notes: [staging] probe_dpu_os_all enqueues probe_dpu_os_task.delay once per DPU unconditionally; MAX_PARALLEL_PROBES is echoed but parallelism is only bounded externally by Celery worker concurrency. FIX: Same as FEAT-0165: gate enqueue by MAX_PARALLEL_PROBES (batch into waves or use a concurrency-bounded group/queue) so the documented 'up to 10 parallel' is actually enforced by the endpoint. | WO-4 #355: probe-dpu-os-all enqueues in waves of MAX_PARALLEL_PROBES (cap enforced).

feature: Register DPU's host as bare-metal host
user_story: As an operator, I want to register an in-band DPU's host into the Bare Metal tab, so that I can deploy on it.
expected_behavior: POST /dpus/{id}/register-host idempotently creates/links a BareMetalHost record with the host IP from DPU config.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to trigger a complete deploy (init + plan + apply chain), so that I can deploy a single module through the full workflow.
expected_behavior: User submits deploy request. System dispatches init task. On init success, triggers plan; on plan success, triggers apply. Returns orchestrator task ID and chain status.
validation_notes: [staging] deploy_module raises BadRequestError when status=='not_initialized' (requires manual init) and then only calls dispatch_apply — it never dispatches init or plan. The auto init→plan→apply chain lives only in deploy_all orchestration. FIX: Either dispatch the full init→plan→apply event chain from deploy_module (auto-init when not_initialized, then chain plan and apply on success, mirroring deploy_all), or update the spec to match the apply-only behavior; to be Validated-green per the spec, wire the auto-init/plan dispatch chain so a single deploy call drives init→plan→apply.
error_detail: deploy_module raises BadRequestError when status=='not_initialized' (requires manual init) and then only calls dispatch_apply — it never dispatches init or plan. The auto init→plan→apply chain lives only in deploy_all orchestration.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to apply infrastructure changes from a plan, so that I can deploy actual infrastructure.
expected_behavior: User submits apply request with optional auto_approve flag. System enqueues task, changes status to 'applying'. Task runs 'tofu apply', captures outputs, updates module.outputs. Returns task ID and apply results.
validation_notes: [staging] OpenTofuActionRequest defines auto_approve (line 28) but opentofu_apply never reads request.auto_approve and submit_apply has no auto_approve parameter, so the documented optional auto_approve flag has no effect. FIX: Pass request.auto_approve from opentofu_apply into submit_apply (add an auto_approve param to submit_apply) and thread it through create_task/dispatch_apply so the apply task honors the flag (e.g. -auto-approve vs interactive/no-op approval).
error_detail: OpenTofuActionRequest defines auto_approve (line 28) but opentofu_apply never reads request.auto_approve and submit_apply has no auto_approve parameter, so the documented optional auto_approve flag has no effect.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to check connectivity status for all clusters at once, so that I can see which are reachable without waiting for individual tests.
expected_behavior: Probes all registered clusters in parallel with lightweight network checks. Returns connectivity state for each (reachable/unreachable).
validation_notes: clusters.py:batch_connectivity_check delegates to ConnectivityProbeService.probe_all_clusters for parallel lightweight network checks.

user_story: As an operator, I want to test connectivity to a registered cluster, so that I can verify the cluster is reachable before operations.
expected_behavior: Tests kubeconfig access by connecting to the cluster's API server. Returns connection status with details about failures (auth, network, certificate).
validation_notes: clusters.py:test_cluster_connection (require_cluster_owner) delegates to KubernetesService.test_connection returning connection status/failure detail.

user_story: As an operator, I want to register and manage Kubernetes clusters (EKS, AKS, GKE, on-prem), so that I can deploy and manage F5 BNK across multiple clusters.
expected_behavior: Create clusters via kubeconfig/EKS auto-detect, test connectivity, refresh kubeconfig, update cluster config, list clusters globally or per-project, delete registrations. Cluster scans auto-enqueued after registration/update.
validation_notes: clusters.py provides add/list-all/list-project/get/update/delete + detect-eks; create_cluster and update both enqueue_cluster_scan as documented.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all Custom Resource Definitions installed in a cluster, so that I can understand what extensions are available.
expected_behavior: Lists installed CRDs merged with a static registry. Supports filtering by API group. Returns CRD metadata including versions and scope.
validation_notes: crds.py:get_cluster_crds delegates to CrdDiscoveryService.list_crds with optional repeatable ?group= filter; 503 NETWORK_UNREACHABLE on unreachable cluster.

user_story: As an operator, I want to create, read, update, delete, patch, label, and annotate any Kubernetes resource, so that I can manage cluster configuration programmatically.
expected_behavior: Full CRUD on any resource type (core API, CRDs, custom resources). Supports namespace-scoped and cluster-wide. Handles label/annotation management and patching.
validation_notes: resources.py get/create/update/patch/delete/label/annotate cover any resource type (core+CRD), namespace-scoped and cluster-wide, with strategic/merge/json patch strategies.

user_story: As an operator, I want to refresh a cluster's kubeconfig, so that I can update credentials for EKS (via AWS CLI) or on-prem clusters (via SSH probe).
expected_behavior: Pulls fresh kubeconfig from AWS CLI for EKS or via SSH probe for on-prem. Automatically triggers cluster scan after refresh.
validation_notes: clusters.py:refresh_cluster_kubeconfig delegates to ClusterManagementService.refresh_kubeconfig (EKS via AWS CLI / on-prem SSH) and enqueue_cluster_scan after.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all namespaces and node counts in a cluster, so that I can understand cluster topology and resource distribution.
expected_behavior: Lists all namespaces and counts nodes. Returns namespace names and node count for capacity planning.
validation_notes: clusters.py:list_cluster_namespaces returns namespace objects+count; node count served by adjacent get_cluster_node_count endpoint.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see a graph of services, pods, and deployments in a namespace, so that I can understand application topology and dependencies.
expected_behavior: Returns topology graph with nodes (services, pods, deployments) and edges (selects, owns). Handles large namespaces with truncation + info message.
validation_notes: topology.py:get_cluster_topology -> build_namespace_topology returns nodes/edges (selects/owns); truncates at _POD_TRUNCATION_THRESHOLD=300 with non-null info message.

user_story: As an operator, I want to cordon, uncordon, and drain nodes, so that I can perform maintenance with minimal impact.
expected_behavior: Cordon (prevent new pods), uncordon (resume scheduling), drain (safely evict workloads before maintenance).
validation_notes: resources.py:cordon_node/uncordon_node/drain_node (require_cluster_owner) delegate to KubernetesService equivalents; drain supports ignore_daemonsets/force/grace_period.

user_story: As an operator, I want to manage pod restart, deployment scaling, and rollout operations, so that I can perform operational tasks without kubectl.
expected_behavior: Restart pods/deployments, scale deployments, view rollout history/status, undo rollouts, get pod metrics (top), view container information.
validation_notes: resources.py:restart_pod/rollout_restart/scale_deployment/rollout_history/rollout_status/rollout_undo + get_pod_metrics + list_pod_containers cover the documented workload management surface.

user_story: As an operator, I want to open an interactive terminal in a pod to debug issues, so that I can execute commands and troubleshoot in real-time.
expected_behavior: WebSocket for interactive pod shell access. Supports stdin/stdout/stderr, terminal resize, graceful termination. Handles shell detection (distroless/minimal containers).
validation_notes: k8s_websocket.py:pod_exec_websocket validates token, opens connect_get_namespaced_pod_exec with stdin/stdout/stderr, handles resize (channel 4) and distroless/no-shell detection.

user_story: As an operator, I want to follow pod logs in real-time, so that I can monitor application behavior and debug issues.
expected_behavior: WebSocket for real-time pod log streaming with tail lines support. Sends logs as they arrive, handles stream buffering for incomplete lines.
validation_notes: k8s_websocket.py:pod_logs_follow_websocket streams logs with follow=True and tail_lines query; line_buffer handles chunks that split mid-line.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see count and health status for all major resource types in a cluster, so that I can get a quick overview from the sidebar.
expected_behavior: Fetches resource counts and health for workloads, networking, Gateway API, storage, cluster resources. Returns health indicators per kind.
validation_notes: resources.py:get_cluster_resource_summary parallel-fetches a fixed kind set (workloads/networking/Gateway API/storage/cluster), computing unhealthy only for health-checkable kinds; TTL-cached.

user_story: As a cluster operator, I want to explore and manage Kubernetes resources across clusters, so that I can observe and modify running workloads
expected_behavior: Project/cluster selector, resource type sidebar (pods, deployments, services), resource table with status, namespace filter, detail panel with metadata/labels/events. Helm releases tab integrated.
validation_notes: KubernetesV2.tsx wires K8sSidebar/K8sResourceTable/K8sDetailPanel + K8sHelmReleasesTable and K8sHelmChartBrowser; project/cluster selector and namespace filter present.

user_story: As a DevOps engineer, I want to browse and install Helm charts directly in the Kubernetes explorer, so that I can manage application deployments
expected_behavior: Chart repository browser, search, chart preview, install dialog with values editor.
validation_notes: K8sHelmChartBrowser.tsx plus components/helm InstallChartDialog/UpgradeReleaseDialog/RollbackReleaseDialog provide browse/search/preview/install-with-values-editor.

user_story: As an operator, I want to activate or switch F5 licenses, so that I can apply paid or renewed licenses to a cluster.
expected_behavior: Submits raw JWT; sends to CWC /reactivate via operator dispatch or legacy. Can activate eval, switch eval->paid, or update existing.
validation_notes: activate_license_endpoint tries operator dispatch (cwc_license_activate) then legacy _cwc_request → activate_license which POSTs raw JWT to /reactivate and infers success from state deltas. Logic matches; needs a live CWC/cluster.

feature: Check CWC Connectivity and Cert Status
user_story: As an operator, I want to diagnose CWC connectivity issues, so that I can troubleshoot licensing problems.
expected_behavior: Comprehensive CWC health check: service deployed, mTLS certs, cert-manager, connectivity. Returns cwc_service_found, cwc_reachable, certs_mounted, setup_complete, full status if reachable.
validation_notes: [staging] The legacy fallback returns only boolean flags + message; check_cwc_available only verifies namespace/service/cert existence and never fetches the CWC /status payload, so no raw status is included even when reachable (the operator path can pass extra fields via extra='allow', but the legacy path cannot). FIX: On the legacy reachable path, actually call the CWC REST /status endpoint (via the mTLS certs) and include the raw status payload in the response when cwc_reachable is true, rather than only returning existence-derived boolean flags. | WO-4 #354: legacy reachable path now includes the raw CWC /status payload.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to check if CWC API mTLS setup is complete, so that I can know if licensing API is ready.
expected_behavior: Returns setup_complete, cert_manager_available, server_cert_exists, client_cert_exists, certs_mounted.
validation_notes: get_cwc_setup_status_endpoint tries operator dispatch (cwc_check_status) then legacy check_setup_status, returning setup_complete/cert_manager_available/server_cert_exists/client_cert_exists/certs_mounted. Matches; needs live cluster.

user_story: As an operator, I want to download the telemetry report for F5 licensing, so that I can send it to F5 for registration.
expected_behavior: Queries CWC for telemetry report (only when 'Config Report Ready to Download'). Returns raw report. Tries operator dispatch first, falls back to legacy.
validation_notes: get_license_report_endpoint tries operator dispatch (cwc_license_report) first then legacy get_license_report which GETs /report; returns raw report (success raises 502 on failure). Matches; CWC gating of 'report ready' is enforced server-side.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check the F5 license status for a cluster, so that I can verify licensing compliance.
expected_behavior: Queries CWC for license and telemetry status. Tries operator dispatch first, falls back to legacy kubeconfig. Returns license status, telemetry state, expiration. Error if CWC unreachable.
validation_notes: get_license_status_endpoint tries operator dispatch (cwc_license_status) then legacy get_license_status which GETs /status and normalizes license_state/telemetry_state/expiry; raises 502 on failure. Matches; needs live CWC.

user_story: As an operator, I want to send signed license manifests back to CWC, so that I can complete the F5 licensing workflow.
expected_behavior: Submits raw signed manifest string; sends to CWC /receipt endpoint. Returns success/failure.
validation_notes: post_license_receipt_endpoint tries operator dispatch (cwc_license_receipt) then legacy post_license_receipt which POSTs raw manifest to /receipt and detects empty/silent rejection. Matches; needs live CWC.

user_story: As an operator, I want to renew F5 licenses (eval or paid), so that I can extend licensing validity.
expected_behavior: Submits JWT and force flag. Default: clean license switch (no downtime, JWKS validation+patching, JWT persistence). Force: nuclear renewal (delete CPCL secrets, restart CWC pod, reactivate; ~2min downtime).
validation_notes: renew_license_endpoint routes force=False→cwc_license_renew(60s)/switch_license (clean) and force=True→cwc_license_force_renew(180s)/force_renew_license (delete CPCL secrets, restart pod, reactivate), with legacy fallback. Matches; needs live cluster.

user_story: As an operator, I want to perform one-time cert-manager setup for CWC mTLS, so that I can enable CWC REST API licensing.
expected_behavior: Runs cert-manager setup: creates certs, patches CWC pod, waits for injection. Tries operator dispatch (180s timeout), falls back to legacy. Idempotent.
validation_notes: [staging] run_cwc_setup_endpoint dispatches cwc_setup_certs with timeout=120.0; the documented 180s timeout actually applies only to the force-renew path. Pure doc/nuance mismatch — setup is functional. FIX: Trivial: either bump the cwc_setup_certs dispatch timeout to 180.0 to match the documented value, or correct the doc to state the setup dispatch uses a 120s timeout (180s is force-renew). | WO-4 #354 (doc): CWC setup dispatch timeout is 120s; the 180s applies to force-renew.

user_story: As an operator, I want to fix invalid JWKS configurations, so that I can resolve licensing failures.
expected_behavior: Checks cpcl-key-cm ConfigMap for valid JWKS, patches with real F5 public keys if needed. Idempotent.
validation_notes: validate_jwks_endpoint calls ensure_valid_jwks directly (no operator dispatch): reads cpcl-key-cm ConfigMap, validates modulus, patches with F5 JWKS (live fetch then F5_STATIC_JWKS fallback), idempotent (returns valid early). Matches; needs live cluster.

user_story: As a developer, I want to connect my AI assistant (Claude Desktop, VS Code) to BNK-Forge via MCP, so that I can leverage AI tools for operations
expected_behavior: Shows MCP connection info, setup guides for various AI assistants, tool catalog with descriptions, health status badge.
validation_notes: pages/MCP.tsx renders connection info, setup guides (Claude Desktop/VS Code/etc.), tool catalog with descriptions, and MCPStatusBadge health status.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check if a newer version of the module library is available, so that I can decide when to sync updates.
expected_behavior: Compares local synced VERSION file with remote GitHub VERSION. Returns synced_version, latest_version, update_available, last_synced_at.
validation_notes: module_library.py:get_module_library_version reads synced_version/last_synced_at/git_ref/git_url from ApplicationSetting, fetches the remote VERSION via raw.githubusercontent with GitAuthService headers, and returns synced_version/latest_version/update_available/last_synced_at.

user_story: As a user, I want to add a custom module from a git repository to my catalog, so that I can use it in projects.
expected_behavior: Validates git source, extracts metadata, parses README, creates ModuleLibrary record with is_official=false.
validation_notes: module_library.py:create_user_module → user_module_service.py:create_user_module validates the git source, extracts metadata, parses README for description, and creates a ModuleLibrary row with is_official=False; duplicate git_source is rejected.

user_story: As a user, I want to remove a user module from my catalog, so that unused modules are cleaned up.
expected_behavior: Deletes ModuleLibrary record if not in use by any projects. Prevents deletion of official modules.
validation_notes: module_library.py:delete_user_module 404s if missing, blocks official modules (ForbiddenError), and refuses deletion when module.project_modules is non-empty, returning an in-use error.

user_story: As a user, I want to extract variables and dependencies from a git repository without adding it to the catalog, so that I can preview what I'm adding.
expected_behavior: Clones repo, parses variables.tf/outputs.tf, extracts provider requirements, parses README. Returns variables_schema, outputs_schema, dependencies, description.
validation_notes: module_library.py:extract_module_metadata → user_module_service.py:extract_module_metadata clones, parses variables.tf/outputs.tf/main.tf/versions.tf and README, and returns variables/outputs/dependencies/provider/description (response keys renamed to variables/outputs but content matches).

user_story: As a user, I want to view detailed information about a module, so that I can understand its purpose and requirements.
expected_behavior: Returns full metadata: variables_schema, outputs, dependencies, provider, compatibility platforms, required capabilities, engine type, git source URL.
validation_notes: module_library.py:get_module returns variables_schema, dependencies, provider, compatibility (via _serialize_module_compatibility), engine metadata (serialize_engine_metadata), and git_source for the requested module.

user_story: As a user, I want to see all input variables for a module, so that I can prepare values for deployment.
expected_behavior: Returns variables with name, type, description, required, sensitive, default, example. Filters out platform-injected variables (project_name, environment, common_tags).
validation_notes: module_library.py:get_module_variables builds variables from inputs_metadata/variables_schema and filters out platform-injected vars {project_name, environment, common_tags}; falls back to VariableParser git parse when no metadata.

user_story: As a user, I want intelligent default values suggested for a module based on my project context, so that I can deploy faster with sensible starting values.
expected_behavior: Generates context-aware defaults: resource names from project name, CIDR blocks, region from project, cloud-provider-specific values, sensible booleans.
validation_notes: module_library.py:get_smart_defaults derives resource names from project slug, CIDR blocks by name pattern, AWS region from project, IBM cred-template inheritance, and sensible booleans/numbers, returning a name→default map.

user_story: As a user, I want to see what module categories are available with counts, so that I can filter my module search effectively.
expected_behavior: Returns category names (infra, k8s, bnk, app, other) with module count each, sorted by count descending.
validation_notes: [staging] get_categories runs a group_by(category) with no ORDER BY, so categories are returned in DB/arbitrary order rather than sorted by count descending. FIX: Add an explicit ordering by count descending — e.g. .order_by(func.count(ModuleLibrary.id).desc()) on the query (or sort the result list by 'count' before caching/returning). | WO-4 #353: categories sorted by count desc.

user_story: As a user, I want to see what cloud providers are supported with module counts, so that I can find provider-specific modules.
expected_behavior: Returns provider names (aws, azure, gcp, on-prem) with module count each, sorted by count descending.
validation_notes: [staging] get_providers runs a group_by(provider) (filtering null providers) with no ORDER BY, so providers are not sorted by count descending. FIX: Add .order_by(func.count(ModuleLibrary.id).desc()) to the providers query (or sort the result list by 'count' descending before caching/returning). | WO-4 #353: providers sorted by count desc.

user_story: As a user, I want to browse available modules in the library, so that I can find modules to add to my project.
expected_behavior: Returns paginated modules filterable by category (infra/k8s/bnk), provider, official_only, tested_only. Includes variables, compatibility, engine type, tags.
validation_notes: module_library.py:list_modules → module_catalog_service.py:get_catalog_modules filters by category/provider/official_only/tested_only and returns variables, compatibility, engine metadata, and tags per module (cached 15min). Returns a modules+total dict (no offset/limit pagination).

user_story: As a user, I want to see available versions (branches/tags) for a user module, so that I can upgrade or switch versions.
expected_behavior: Queries git repo for branches and tags. Returns current_version and arrays of available branches and tags.
validation_notes: [staging] The route's own query filters with `not ModuleLibrary.is_official`, a Python boolean negation of a Column that evaluates to the literal False, so the filter becomes `... , False` and always returns no row — every non-official module 404s. (The service path user_module_service.list_module_versions at line 618 queries by id only and is unaffected, but the cited route is broken.) FIX: Replace `not ModuleLibrary.is_official` with a real SQL predicate, e.g. `ModuleLibrary.is_official.is_(False)` (or `== False`), so the lookup actually matches non-official modules. | WO-4 #350: filter now ModuleLibrary.is_official.is_(False) — user modules resolve.

user_story: As an operator, I want to manually sync the official BNK-Forge module catalog, so that new modules are available immediately.
expected_behavior: Clones official module repo, parses all modules, extracts metadata, updates ModuleLibrary records. Returns added/updated/skipped statistics.
validation_notes: module_library.py:sync_catalog → module_catalog_service.py:sync_module_catalog clones the official repo, parses modules, updates ModuleLibrary, and returns stats; cache invalidated after sync.

user_story: As a user, I want to update a user module to a different version, so that I can get bug fixes and new features.
expected_behavior: Checks out new version, re-extracts metadata, updates ModuleLibrary record. Returns success with new version.
validation_notes: module_library.py:update_module_version → user_module_service.py:update_module_version validates the new ref, re-extracts metadata (vars/deps/provider/description/readme), updates git_source+version, and resets test status; blocks official modules.

feature: Validate Git Source for User Module
user_story: As a user, I want to validate that a git repository contains valid Terraform code, so that I can verify it before adding to the catalog.
expected_behavior: Clones repo, checks for *.tf files, verifies main.tf, lists branches/tags. Returns validation result and Terraform files found.
validation_notes: module_library.py:validate_git_source → user_module_service.py:validate_git_source clones (depth=1), walks for *.tf/*.hcl, requires a main.tf, lists branches, and returns valid + terraform_files + available_refs.

user_story: As an operator, I want to add a new module source repository, so that modules from new sources can be discovered.
expected_behavior: Creates ModuleSource with git/registry/builtin type, URL, optional authentication, auto-sync settings, description.
validation_notes: module_sources.py:create_module_source → module_source_service.py:create_source validates source_type (git/registry/builtin), encrypts auth_token, normalizes credential metadata per provider, persists auto_sync/sync_interval/description, and triggers initial git sync.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove a module source, so that unused repositories are no longer synced.
expected_behavior: Deletes ModuleSource and cascades to delete associated ModuleLibrary entries.
validation_notes: module_source_service.py:delete_source blocks builtin sources, refuses deletion when child ModuleLibrary entries are in use by projects (SOURCE_IN_USE), and otherwise cascade-deletes all catalog modules for the source. The in-use guard is stricter than the docs' plain 'cascades' but is an additive safety check, not a defect.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see all configured module sources, so that I can understand what repositories feed the module catalog.
expected_behavior: Returns paginated sources with URL, sync status, last_synced_at, module count, auth type, credential scope, auto-sync config.
validation_notes: module_source_service.py:list_sources/_serialize_source returns url, sync_status, last_synced_at, module_count, auth_type, credential_type/scope, and auto_sync config; filterable by source_type/is_active.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see what modules are available from a specific source, so that I can audit module catalog contents.
expected_behavior: Returns paginated ModuleLibrary records associated with a ModuleSource with all metadata.
validation_notes: module_source_service.py:list_source_modules returns active ModuleLibrary rows for the source with id/name/category/provider/description/source_path/version/update metadata.

user_story: As an operator, I want to manually sync a module source, so that new modules are discovered immediately.
expected_behavior: Clones git repo, discovers Terraform modules, parses metadata, creates/updates ModuleLibrary records. Returns sync statistics.
validation_notes: module_sources.py:sync_module_source → module_source_service.py:sync_source delegates git sources to ModuleSyncService.sync_git_source (clone, discover, parse, upsert ModuleLibrary) plus auto-sync of linked blueprints, returning sync statistics; registry sources refresh upstream version metadata.

user_story: As an operator, I want to update a module source configuration, so that I can change its URL, auth, or auto-sync settings.
expected_behavior: Updates name, URL, branch, git_ref, auth credentials, credential type, auto_sync, sync_interval_hours.
validation_notes: module_source_service.py:update_source updates name/url/branch/git_ref, re-encrypts auth_token, resolves credential_type/auth_type, and updates auto_sync/sync_interval_hours; builtin sources are immutable.

user_story: As an operator, I want to verify that credentials for a private module source are valid, so that sync operations will succeed.
expected_behavior: Tests provided credentials (token, SSH key, basic auth) against the git repo or registry. Returns validation status and error details.
validation_notes: module_source_service.py:validate_source_credentials runs provider-specific git ls-remote / API checks for github_app, gitlab, ssh_deploy_key, and oauth_token, persists validation status/error and audit logs. Note: legacy_pat/service_account_token/none are explicitly rejected as 'not implemented in this slice'.

user_story: As a system service, I want to programmatically create notifications, so that users are informed of important events.
expected_behavior: POST /api/notifications creates new notification; user field defaults to current user if not specified; stores type, title, message, optional resource reference.
validation_notes: notifications.py:create_notification defaults user to JWT username when unset and stores type/title/message/resource refs.

user_story: As a user, I want to delete individual notifications, so that I can manage my notification history.
expected_behavior: DELETE /api/notifications/{id} deletes notification; returns success.
validation_notes: notifications.py:delete_notification deletes by id and returns {success:true}.

user_story: As a user, I want to retrieve my notifications and filter by read status or limit, so that I can stay informed.
expected_behavior: GET /api/notifications returns notifications for current user or 'all'; unread_only filter; ordered by created_at desc; supports limit.
validation_notes: notifications.py:get_notifications returns rows for effective user OR 'all', unread_only filter, ordered created_at desc with limit.

user_story: As a user, I want to quickly check how many unread notifications I have, so that I can prioritize checking the notification center.
expected_behavior: GET /api/notifications/unread-count returns count of unread notifications for current user.
validation_notes: notifications.py:get_unread_count counts unread for current user or 'all'.

user_story: As a user, I want to mark all my unread notifications as read at once, so that I can clear my notification inbox.
expected_behavior: POST /api/notifications/mark-all-read marks all unread notifications for current user as read; returns count marked.
validation_notes: notifications.py:mark_all_read marks all unread for the user as read and returns count marked.

user_story: As a user, I want to mark individual notifications as read, so that I can track which ones I've reviewed.
expected_behavior: PATCH /api/notifications/{id}/read marks notification is_read=True, read_at=now; returns success.
validation_notes: notifications.py:mark_notification_read sets is_read=True and read_at=now (only if currently unread).

user_story: As a dashboard client, I want to receive real-time deployment status updates via WebSocket, so that I see progress without polling.
expected_behavior: WS /api/notifications/ws/deployments accepts client connections; receives messages with deployment_id, status (running/success/failed/cancelled), resource_changes, error_message; ping/pong keepalive.
validation_notes: notifications.py:websocket_deployment_notifications accepts clients, broadcasts deployment_id/status/resource_changes/error_message, with ping/pong keepalive (30s timeout).

user_story: As an admin, I want to manually trigger cleanup of disconnected operators, so that I can prune stale entries.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/cleanup-stale marks operators with heartbeat >2m old as disconnected, expires queued commands.
validation_notes: cleanup_stale (crud.py:110, admin-guarded) calls cleanup_stale_operators (120s = STALE_HEARTBEAT_THRESHOLD, operator_registry.py:38/245) and cleanup_expired_commands.

user_story: As an operator, I want to send a command to multiple operators at once (by ID or labels), so that I can coordinate fleet actions.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/fan-out broadcasts command to specified or label-matched operators, returns per-operator results.
validation_notes: fan_out_command (commands.py:76) targets explicit ids, label-matched connected operators, or all, then send_command_to_multiple returns a per-operator results map.

user_story: As an operator, I want to diff BNK configuration between two clusters, so that I can identify topology divergence.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/fleet/compare fetches configs from both clusters, diffs them, returns resource differences.
validation_notes: fleet_compare_configs (fleet.py:760) exports+diffs both clusters' configs returning resource differences, with a health-report diff fallback when clusters aren't accessible.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see the health and status of all clusters across the fleet, so that I can monitor the deployment.
expected_behavior: GET /operators/fleet-health queries all clusters in parallel via kubeconfig, returns aggregated health with DPF status.
validation_notes: get_fleet_health (fleet.py:575) queries clusters in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor (max_workers up to 10) calling _query_cluster_health, which includes DPF status via _query_dpf_summary.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to inspect a specific operator's metadata and health report, so that I can diagnose issues.
expected_behavior: GET /operators/{id} returns operator with connectivity mode, last health report, registration token name.
validation_notes: get_operator_detail (crud.py:58) returns the operator response plus last_health_report and registration_token.name (connectivity mode is included in _operator_to_response).

user_story: As an operator, I want to link an operator to a Kubernetes cluster, so that the engine prefers it for deployments.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/link-cluster sets operator.cluster_id, enforces one-to-one mapping.
validation_notes: link_operator_to_cluster (commands.py:265) sets op.cluster_id and enforces one-to-one by rejecting if another operator already holds that cluster_id.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see available operator connectivity modes, so that I can choose how to connect an operator.
expected_behavior: GET /operators/connectivity-modes returns dict of modes (direct_ws, polling, reverse_ssh) with current status.
validation_notes: list_connectivity_modes (crud.py:49) returns operator_connectivity.get_available_modes (direct_ws/polling/reverse_ssh) with current status.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all registered operators, so that I can monitor their connectivity status.
expected_behavior: GET /operators returns list of ConnectedOperator with cluster_name, status, version, last heartbeat, command stats.
validation_notes: list_all_operators (crud.py:32) returns list_operators mapped through _operator_to_response carrying cluster_name, status, version, heartbeat, and command stats.

user_story: As an operator, I want to open a reverse SSH tunnel for an operator in reverse_ssh mode, so that it can reach the control plane.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/reverse-tunnel/open opens SSH tunnel using configured SSH credential.
validation_notes: open_reverse_tunnel (commands.py:228) requires reverse_ssh mode and opens the tunnel via open_reverse_ssh_tunnel using ssh_credential_id from connectivity_config.

user_story: As a polling operator, I want to fetch pending commands, so that I can execute them without WebSocket.
expected_behavior: GET /operators/{id}/poll returns queued commands (max 5), marks them picked_up, updates heartbeat.
validation_notes: poll_commands (operator_polling.py:168) updates last_heartbeat_at, returns up to .limit(5) QUEUED commands marking them PICKED_UP (and expiring timed-out ones).

user_story: As an operator, I want to preview the install command before committing, so that I can verify the setup.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/connectivity/preview returns helm install command + kubectl apply without persisting.
validation_notes: preview_connectivity_setup (commands.py:193) returns resolve_connectivity output (helm_install_command + kubectl_command + env_vars) without persisting mode.

user_story: As an operator, I want to register an operator using HTTP polling (no WebSocket), so that it works behind restrictive firewalls.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/register-poll creates operator record, returns operator_id for polling endpoints.
validation_notes: register_poll_operator (operator_polling.py:115) creates the ConnectedOperator record and returns operator_id for the polling endpoints.

user_story: As an operator, I want to delete an operator registration, so that I can clean up disconnected operators.
expected_behavior: DELETE /operators/{id} disconnects WebSocket, removes ConnectedOperator record.
validation_notes: remove_operator (crud.py:76) disconnects the live WebSocket if connected and delete_operator removes the ConnectedOperator record.

user_story: As an operator, I want to dispatch a command to a connected operator, so that I can execute cluster actions.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/command sends action+payload to operator via WebSocket, waits for result (up to timeout).
validation_notes: send_operator_command (commands.py:35) requires a connected operator and awaits operator_connections.send_command with action+payload up to body.timeout.

user_story: As an operator, I want to configure how an operator connects (direct WS, polling, reverse SSH), so that I can set up proper tunneling.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/connectivity sets mode, returns install command and env vars for the operator deployment.
validation_notes: set_connectivity_mode (commands.py:142) validates+persists the mode and returns resolve_connectivity setup with install command and env_vars.

user_story: As a polling operator, I want to submit a command's result, so that the control plane knows it completed.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/results/{cmd_id} persists success flag, output_lines, error_message.
validation_notes: submit_result (operator_polling.py:248) persists success flag (COMPLETED/FAILED), output_lines, and error_message and bumps operator command stats.

user_story: As a polling operator, I want to report in-cluster LLM backend metrics, so that usage can be tracked.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/llm-metrics stores namespace/name/data metrics keyed by cluster.
validation_notes: submit_llm_metrics (operator_polling.py:360) stores namespace/name/data via store_llm_metrics keyed by operator/cluster.

user_story: As a polling operator, I want to report cluster and BNK health, so that the control plane tracks status.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/health persists cluster/bnk health dicts to last_health_report.
validation_notes: submit_health (operator_polling.py:332) assembles cluster/bnk dicts and persists them to last_health_report via update_operator_health.

user_story: As a polling operator, I want to send a heartbeat, so that I stay marked as connected.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/heartbeat updates last_heartbeat_at, operator_version, commands_executed.
validation_notes: submit_heartbeat (operator_polling.py:308) calls update_operator_heartbeat updating last_heartbeat_at, operator_version, and commands_executed.

user_story: As an operator, I want to unlink an operator from its cluster, so that deployments can target other operators.
expected_behavior: POST /operators/{id}/unlink-cluster clears operator.cluster_id.
validation_notes: unlink_operator_from_cluster (commands.py:316) clears op.cluster_id and commits.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to deploy all modules in a project sequentially, so that I can provision entire infrastructure in one operation.
expected_behavior: User submits deploy-all. System validates project (no modules in error state), prevents duplicate orchestrators with FOR UPDATE lock, enqueues sequential deployment via dependency layers. Returns orchestrator task ID and execution plan.
validation_notes: deploy_all_modules in routes/project_orchestration.py uses a FOR UPDATE lock to prevent duplicate orchestrators, validates the project, and enqueues layered sequential deployment via deploy_project_parallel.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to destroy all modules in a project in reverse order, so that I can clean up all infrastructure safely.
expected_behavior: User submits destroy-all. System updates all StackInstance records to 'destroying' status. Enqueues sequential destruction in reverse layer order. Returns orchestrator task ID and plan.
validation_notes: destroy_all_modules in routes/project_orchestration.py sets StackInstance records to 'destroying' and enqueues reverse-layer destruction via destroy_project_parallel, returning the orchestrator task ID/plan.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to query all modules across projects with pagination and filtering, so that I can see deployment overview and search modules.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns paginated list of ProjectModule records (default 50 per page, max 200). Supports filtering by project_id and status. Eager-loads project and library module details. Optimized to avoid N+1 queries.
validation_notes: get_all_modules in routes/project_orchestration.py paginates ProjectModule (default 50, max 200), filters by project_id/status, and eager-loads project+library_module with load_only to avoid N+1.

user_story: As an architect, I want to see how modules will be grouped into dependency layers with time estimates, so that I can understand execution strategy and time savings.
expected_behavior: Endpoint calculates execution layers from dependency graph. For each layer: module list, max execution time, can_run_parallel flag. Returns sequential vs parallel time estimates and percentage savings.
validation_notes: get_execution_plan (routes/project_orchestration.py and services/parallel_execution_service.py) computes dependency layers with per-layer max time and can_run_parallel, returning sequential vs parallel estimates and savings percentage.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to check real-time progress of a project deployment, so that I can monitor execution and see which modules are running.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns ParallelExecution record with status, current_layer, total_layers, successful/failed/skipped module lists, timing, and progress percentage. Calculates progress as current_layer / total_layers.
validation_notes: get_parallel_execution_status in routes/project_orchestration.py returns the ParallelExecution record with current_layer/total_layers, success/fail/skip lists, timing, and progress as current_layer/total_layers.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see recent deployment/destruction operations for a project, so that I can review execution history.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns paginated list of ParallelExecution records ordered by created_at descending. Includes action, status, layer info, timing, module counts, triggered_by.
validation_notes: list_parallel_executions in routes/project_orchestration.py returns a paginated list ordered by created_at desc with action, status, layer info, timing, module counts, and triggered_by.

user_story: As a platform engineer, I want to run performance benchmarks comparing proxy implementations (envoy, nginx, haproxy, BNK, nodeport), so that I can validate proxy performance
expected_behavior: Targets tab (target CRUD, proxy deployment), Configs tab (config CRUD, JSON editor), Agents tab (agent list, getting started), Runs tab (runs table, filters, comparison checkboxes), Compare tab (side-by-side metrics with winner indicators).
source: pages/Benchmarks.tsx, pages/BenchmarkTargetsTab.tsx, pages/BenchmarkConfigsTab.tsx, pages/BenchmarkAgentsTab.tsx, pages/BenchmarkRunsTab.tsx, pages/BenchmarkRunDetail.tsx, pages/BenchmarkCompareTab.tsx
validation_notes: pages/Benchmarks.tsx wires Targets/Configs/Agents/Runs/Detail/Compare tabs to their respective tab components matching the documented UI.

user_story: As an operator, I want to set the currently active project, so that UI and CLI default to the correct deployment context.
expected_behavior: User sets a project as active (is_active=true). Only one project can be active at a time. System updates is_active flags atomically.
validation_notes: Route activate_project (routes/projects.py:155) calls ProjectService.set_active_project (project_service.py:666), which deactivates only currently-active projects via filter (is_active AND id!=project_id) then activates the target atomically in one commit.

user_story: As a platform operator, I want to create a new project with type and cloud provider inference, so that I can organize infrastructure deployment efforts.
expected_behavior: User creates a project specifying name, type (cloud-aws/cloud-azure/cloud-gcp/cloud-ibm/kubernetes), region, and optional credential template. System resolves cloud provider from type, binds default credentials if none specified, and initializes state encryption. Returns project ID and metadata.
validation_notes: [staging] The route calls ProjectService.create_project, which only forwards project_data.credential_template_id (line 474) with no default-template resolution; the default-binding logic (_resolve_default_template_id) lives only in the unused ProjectCRUDService.create_project (line 78-79), so projects can be created with no credentials bound. FIX: In ProjectService.create_project, when credential_template_id is None resolve and bind the default credential template (matching cloud_provider, else the global is_default) before constructing the Project — reusing ProjectCRUDService._resolve_default_template_id, or consolidate the two create_project paths. | WO-4 #351: ProjectService.create_project binds provider-matched is_default template.

user_story: As an architect, I want to declare that one project depends on outputs from another, so that dependent infrastructure receives outputs from prerequisite projects.
expected_behavior: User specifies dependent_projects list with project IDs and output names to wire. System stores dependency metadata. Execution validates cross-project outputs exist before deploying dependent modules.
validation_notes: update_dependencies in services/project_service.py validates dependent projects exist, checks for circular cross-project dependencies, and stores the dependency metadata as JSON.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to remove a project permanently, so that I can clean up unused infrastructure deployments.
expected_behavior: Owner deletes project after checking it's not locked by active operations. Cascades deletion to all modules and their state. Requires explicit force flag if project is currently active or only project.
validation_notes: delete_project in services/project_service.py checks active/only-project status (requiring force), validates workspace locks, and cascades module/state deletion before commit.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to fetch detailed metadata for a specific project, so that I can understand its configuration and state.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns full project configuration including backend settings, encryption config, cloud provider settings, infrastructure access details, and cross-project dependencies.
validation_notes: get_project_detail in services/project_service.py returns full config (backend settings, encryption, cloud provider, infra access, cross-project deps) via _project_to_detail_dict.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all available projects with their status summaries, so that I can navigate and manage multiple deployments.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns paginated list of all projects with counts of total modules, deployed modules, and failed modules. Includes project metadata (name, type, cloud provider, region, owner).
validation_notes: list_projects in services/project_service.py returns a list with module_count/deployed_count/failed_count and metadata (name, type, provider, region, owner).

user_story: As a project owner, I want to transfer ownership to another user, so that team members can manage the project independently.
expected_behavior: Owner transfers project to another user by ID. System updates user_id. New owner gains full permissions. Returns ownership transfer confirmation.
validation_notes: transfer_ownership in services/project_service.py validates the new owner exists/is active, updates user_id, and records an audit log with before/after ownership.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to modify project metadata (name, description, color, icon, environment), so that I can keep configuration current and organized.
expected_behavior: Owner updates project properties. System freezes encryption passphrase if project is renamed and state encryption is enabled. Validates unique name. Returns updated project metadata.
validation_notes: update_project in services/project_service.py freezes the encryption passphrase on rename when state encryption is enabled (_freeze_encryption_passphrase_before_rename), validates unique name, and returns updated metadata.

user_story: As a user managing bare-metal deployments, I want to configure DPU provisioning and kernel bootstrapping, so that I can manage hardware-based deployments
expected_behavior: Bare metal specific configuration panel for DPU hardware and K8s bootstrap management.
validation_notes: BareMetalPanel.tsx exists and is lazy-loaded in ProjectDetailV2.tsx; the bare-metal tab is conditionally rendered when project_type === 'bare-metal' inside a Suspense boundary.

user_story: As an operator, I want to discover and import infrastructure nodes via SSH, so that I can onboard existing resources
expected_behavior: Node discovery UI allowing SSH credential selection and triggering discovery scans. Shows discovered nodes and import workflow.
validation_notes: NodeDiscoveryPanel.tsx is imported and rendered on the discovery tab in ProjectDetailV2.tsx with SSH credential selection and trigger props (canTrigger, jumphost, projectSshCredentialId).

user_story: As a platform operator, I want to view and manage DPU configurations and status, so that I can maintain data plane unit health
expected_behavior: DPU-specific panel showing configuration, resource consumption, and management options for data plane units.
validation_notes: DpuPanel.tsx is lazy-loaded in ProjectDetailV2.tsx; the DPU tab is conditionally shown for kubernetes/bare-metal project types within a Suspense fallback.

user_story: As an operator, I want to detect and reconcile configuration drift, so that infrastructure remains synchronized with desired state
expected_behavior: Drift detection configuration, scheduled checks, history of drift detection runs. Shows resources added/changed/destroyed.
validation_notes: DriftSettings.tsx and DriftCheckHistory.tsx both exist and render on the drift tab in ProjectDetailV2.tsx (lines 726-730), covering config, scheduled checks, and drift run history with resource counts.

user_story: As a user, I want to attach and manage Kubernetes clusters for a project, so that I can target deployments to specific clusters
expected_behavior: List of attached clusters with reachability indicators. Platform mismatch warnings. Add cluster button. Link to full K8s resource page.
validation_notes: K8sClusterList.tsx renders on the clusters tab (ProjectDetailV2.tsx lines 648-683) with reachability badges, platform mismatch warnings, an add-cluster button, and a link to the K8s resource page.

user_story: As a developer, I want to manage IaC modules and deployed blueprints, execute init/plan/apply/destroy operations, and monitor deployment status, so that I can control infrastructure changes
expected_behavior: Full-width module list with dependency pipeline visualization, collapsible sections for standalone/stack-grouped modules. Per-module action buttons (init, plan, apply, destroy, rerun). Status badges, variables editor, rollback, delete. Module detail sheet with outputs, state, variables, logs tabs.
validation_notes: ModuleGroupTable.tsx/ModuleTableRow.tsx provide the full-width module list with dependency pipeline and collapsible standalone/stack-grouped sections plus per-module init/plan/apply/destroy/rerun/delete actions; the module detail sheet exposes Outputs/State/Variables/Logs/History tabs.

user_story: As an operator, I want to manage project secrets and required credentials, so that sensitive data is properly handled
expected_behavior: Secrets manager showing required vs missing secrets by blueprint. Add/edit/delete secret UI. Missing secret count badge on tab.
validation_notes: ProjectSecretsManager.tsx renders on the secrets tab (ProjectDetailV2.tsx lines 639-645) with a dynamic missing-secret count badge that turns red when missing_count > 0.

user_story: As a user, I want to capture and restore infrastructure state snapshots, so that I can safely rollback to known-good configurations
expected_behavior: List of saved state snapshots with creation time. Restore action per snapshot.
validation_notes: SnapshotHistory.tsx renders on the snapshots tab (ProjectDetailV2.tsx lines 733-739) listing saved state snapshots with creation time and a per-snapshot restore action.

user_story: As a user, I want to browse all projects with filters, search, and ownership visibility, so that I can find and manage my deployments
expected_behavior: Sidebar with status filters (active/inactive/failed), ownership filter (all/mine), quick stats. Compact table showing project name, status, type/location, module counts, deployed/failed badges, drift count, last activity time.
validation_notes: Projects.tsx provides the sidebar status filters (active/inactive/failed) and ownership filter (all/mine) with quick stats, plus a compact table showing name, status, type/location, module counts, deployed/failed badges, drift count, and last activity; CreateProjectDialog is imported and rendered.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to check if the CWC QKView API is available on a cluster, so that I know if I can collect diagnostics.
expected_behavior: Checks CWC API reachability. Tries operator dispatch first, falls back to legacy ephemeral pod approach. Returns availability status and dispatch method.
validation_notes: qkview.py:check_cwc tries operator dispatch (cwc_check_status, sets operator_dispatch=True) then falls back to legacy check_cwc_available ephemeral-pod path; returns availability + dispatch method.

user_story: As an operator, I want to cancel running QKView jobs or delete completed collections, so that I can manage cluster resources.
expected_behavior: Cancels running QKView job or deletes completed collection. Prevents deletion of in-progress jobs (returns 409).
validation_notes: [staging] delete_qkview_endpoint (and cancel) have no @handle_route_errors; the legacy delete_qkview raises QKViewError(status_code=409) for in-progress jobs, but QKViewError is a plain Exception not registered with any handler, so it falls through to general_exception_handler which always returns HTTP 500 (ignoring status_code). FIX: Translate QKViewError to its status_code — e.g. register a FastAPI exception handler for QKViewError that emits exc.status_code, or have the legacy fallback in delete_qkview_endpoint catch QKViewError and re-raise HTTPException(status_code=exc.status_code or 500, ...) (mirroring the operator branch's 409 handling). | WO-4 #352: legacy QKView delete/cancel translate QKViewError(409) to HTTP 409.

user_story: As an operator, I want to clean up ephemeral QKView pods, so that I can remove legacy client pods from the cluster.
expected_behavior: Removes all bnk-forge-agent ephemeral curl pods. With operator dispatch, ephemeral pods are no longer created.
validation_notes: qkview.py:cleanup_pods_endpoint delegates to qkview_service.cleanup_client_pods to remove bnk-forge-agent ephemeral curl pods; docstring notes operator dispatch no longer creates them.

user_story: As an operator, I want to create QKView diagnostic collections from a cluster, so that I can collect diagnostic data for support.
expected_behavior: Creates QKView collection job with optional namespace, pod patterns, core file collection, filename. Returns job ID and status. Dispatches via operator or ephemeral pod.
validation_notes: qkview.py:create_qkview_endpoint builds namespace/filename/pod_patterns/core-files payload, tries operator (cwc_qkview_create), else legacy create_qkview; returns id/filename/status.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to download a completed QKView tarball, so that I can share diagnostics with support.
expected_behavior: Downloads QKView tarball via operator (base64-decoded) or ephemeral pod. Returns as gzip file attachment.
validation_notes: [staging] If the operator dispatch returns success but omits binary=True, the `if result.get('binary')` block is skipped without returning, so execution falls through to the legacy ephemeral-pod download path and re-does the work. Harmless in practice (operator always sets binary on download) but a real logic gap. FIX: After a successful operator result, do not fall through: either return the operator data unconditionally (decoding when binary is set), or raise an error/log when a successful operator download lacks binary, so the legacy path only runs when the operator path was not taken at all. | WO-4 #357: operator download branch is terminal (no fall-through to legacy).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all QKView jobs and their status, so that I can monitor diagnostic collection progress.
expected_behavior: Lists all QKView jobs on cluster with IDs, status, filenames. Gets individual job details and status (pending/running/completed).
validation_notes: qkview.py:list_qkviews_endpoint/get_qkview_endpoint/get_qkview_status_endpoint each prefer operator dispatch then legacy list/get/status; list returns ids/status/filenames.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check if a newer version is available for an imported module, so that I can stay up to date.
expected_behavior: Queries registry for latest version. Returns current_version, latest_version, update_available.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:check_for_updates queries get_module_versions, picks latest via _pick_latest_version, and returns current_version/latest_version/update_available; non-registry modules short-circuit with update_available=False.

user_story: As a user, I want to see details of a registry module, so that I can understand its capabilities before importing.
expected_behavior: Returns module metadata: description, provider documentation, versions available, resource documentation.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:get_module_details GETs /modules/{ns}/{name}/{provider} and returns the registry JSON (description, providers, versions, resources) verbatim; route 404s when absent.

user_story: As a user, I want to see all available versions of a registry module, so that I can choose the right version to import.
expected_behavior: Returns available versions with version string and creation date. Identifies latest version.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:get_module_versions returns the versions array with version+published date; latest identification is performed by _pick_latest_version (semver sort) in callers, and the data is returned as documented.

user_story: As an operator, I want to import a module from a public git URL, so that I can use non-registry modules in my catalog.
expected_behavior: Accepts git URL with ref (tag/branch/commit). Clones, extracts subpath if provided, scrapes variables, synthesizes pack.json, creates ModuleLibrary record.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:import_module_from_git fetches via module_fetcher with url+ref+subpath, derives identity, then _finalize_import scrapes variables and synthesizes pack.json before creating the ModuleLibrary row.

user_story: As an operator, I want to import a module from OpenTofu/Terraform public registry, so that I can use it in my catalog.
expected_behavior: Fetches module tarball, extracts to local catalog, scrapes variables/outputs, synthesizes pack.json, creates ModuleLibrary record.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:import_module_from_registry fetches the tarball, then _finalize_import writes the local catalog, scrapes variables+outputs, synthesizes pack.json, and persists ModuleLibrary.

user_story: As an operator, I want to import a private module from Terraform Cloud, so that I can use proprietary modules in my catalog.
expected_behavior: Uses credential template's TFC token to authenticate. Fetches private module, scrapes variables, synthesizes pack.json, creates ModuleLibrary record.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:import_module_from_tfc loads the CloudCredentialTemplate, decrypts its TFC token, fetches the private module with that token, and finalizes via the shared scrape+synthesize+persist path; missing template/token and decrypt failure are guarded.

user_story: As a user, I want to search for modules in public registries, so that I can find official Terraform/OpenTofu modules.
expected_behavior: Searches OpenTofu and Terraform registries with query, optional provider filter, verified flag. Returns module list with name, provider, description, download URL.
validation_notes: registry_service.py:search_modules queries both OpenTofu and Terraform registries with q/provider/verified params and returns the module list+meta (name, provider, description, download URL).

user_story: As an operator, I want to upgrade an imported module to a newer version, so that I get bug fixes and new features.
expected_behavior: Fetches new version, re-extracts, re-scrapes variables, updates ModuleLibrary record. Preserves user metadata overrides.
validation_notes: [staging] upgrade_module permits source_type=tfc_private at the guard (line 476) but unconditionally raises ValueError for tfc_private (line 489), so TFC modules report update_available=True via check_for_updates yet can never be upgraded. Separately, metadata_overrides is only read (line 269) and is never written by any code, so the 'preserves user metadata overrides' path is dead. FIX: Implement the tfc_private upgrade path (re-fetch via fetch_tfc_private using the stored credential template, as import does) instead of always raising; and either populate metadata_overrides somewhere (e.g. capture user edits on import/update) or remove the dead 'preserves overrides' claim if overrides are never set. | WO-4 #353 (doc): TFC modules upgrade via re-import (/api/registry/import-tfc); metadata_overrides preservation is not wired.

user_story: As a user, I want to run a diagnostic runbook against my cluster, so that I can identify and resolve issues.
expected_behavior: Executes all runbook steps sequentially against specified cluster. Returns step-by-step results with status (pass/fail/skip), message, details, optional resource links.
validation_notes: runbooks.py:run_runbook → runbook_service.py:execute_runbook runs every step sequentially against the cluster (a failed step does not halt the rest) and returns per-step status (pass/fail/skip), message, details, and optional resource_link.

user_story: As a user, I want to see available diagnostic runbooks, so that I can troubleshoot cluster issues.
expected_behavior: Returns runbook definitions with id, name, description, category, step_count. Each step includes name, description, expected outcomes.
validation_notes: runbooks.py:get_runbooks → runbook_service.py:list_runbooks returns id/name/description/category/step_count with per-step name+description; documented per-step 'expected outcomes' (pass/fail messages) exist on the step model but are intentionally omitted from list output.

user_story: As a user, I want to upload credentials/certificates/config files, so that I can inject them into module execution.
expected_behavior: Uploads file with name, optional description, target module path/variable; base64-encodes, encrypts, stores with filename/size/mime. Supports arbitrary file types.
validation_notes: create_file_secret reads upload, base64-encodes then encrypts content, stores filename/file_size/mime_type via _upsert_secret (reactivates soft-deleted same-name rows); accepts any content type.

user_story: As a user, I want to store API keys/passwords/tokens as secrets, so that I can use them safely in modules.
expected_behavior: Submits name, value, optional description and target; encrypts value, stores. Value never returned in list operations.
validation_notes: create_value_secret encrypts the value via encrypt_value and stores with optional description/target; list_secrets never includes the value (only file metadata or decrypted value when include_values=True, not used by the list route).

user_story: As a user, I want to remove secrets from my project, so that I can clean up unused credentials.
expected_behavior: Soft-deletes secret (is_active=false). Returns success or NotFoundError.
validation_notes: delete_secret sets is_active=False (soft delete) and returns False if not found; route raises NotFoundError on False and commits.

user_story: As a user, I want to clear secret values from stack variables, so that I can remove deployment-time configuration.
expected_behavior: Submits variable name; sets value to empty string preserving structure. NotFoundError if stack/variable missing.
validation_notes: delete_stack_variable_secret finds latest non-destroyed StackInstance, sets the named variable (flat or nested under module path) to empty string preserving structure, NotFoundError if stack or variable missing.

user_story: As a user, I want to know what secrets are required for a project or stack, so that I can configure missing credentials.
