expected_behavior: Analyzes module inputs (optionally scoped to a stack). Returns required secrets with name/type/module_path/variable_name/required/exists/source/secret_id/guidance. Dedupes by variable_name, merges across modules, caches 60s, includes stack prerequisites.
validation_notes: get_required_secrets analyzes module inputs (optionally scoped by stack_slug), dedupes by variable_name with required-merge logic, returns exists/source/secret_id/guidance, includes stack prerequisites, and caches the result 60s.

user_story: As a user, I want to import F5 FAR pull secrets from various formats, so that I can enable access to F5 container repositories.
expected_behavior: Uploads file (tgz/tar/json/txt) as cne_pull_secret; detects format (docker config JSON, base64, GCP SA JSON), normalizes to base64 docker config with repo.f5.com auth. Creates or updates. Returns action.
validation_notes: import_special_secret(cne_pull_secret) handles tgz/tar/json/txt, _extract_cne_pull_secret_from_text detects docker config JSON / base64 / GCP SA JSON and normalizes to base64 docker config with repo.f5.com auth, creating or updating and returning action.

user_story: As a user, I want to import F5 license JWT tokens from various formats, so that I can store them as project secrets.
expected_behavior: Uploads file (txt/json/jwt) as jwt_token; extracts JWT from text or JSON wrappers, validates three-segment format, stores. Creates or updates. Returns action.
validation_notes: import_special_secret(jwt_token) via _extract_jwt_from_text pulls token from raw text or json wrappers (jwt_token/jwt/token), validates the three-segment dot format, then creates/updates and returns action.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see what secrets are configured for my project, so that I can manage project-level secrets.
expected_behavior: Returns active secrets with metadata (id, name, secret_type, target_module_path, target_variable_name, last_used_at; file secrets add filename/size/mime). Never returns actual values.
validation_notes: list_project_secrets → list_secrets returns active secrets with id/name/secret_type/target_module_path/target_variable_name/last_used_at (file secrets add filename/file_size/mime_type) and never the decrypted value (include_values defaults False).

user_story: As a system, I want to protect sensitive values at rest, so that credentials are never stored in plaintext.
expected_behavior: Service uses AES encryption to encrypt/decrypt all secret values before DB storage; file secrets base64-encoded then encrypted. Decryption only at runtime/update, not during list.
validation_notes: secrets_service encrypts all values via core.encryption.encrypt_value (Fernet AES-128-CBC+HMAC) before storage; file secrets are base64-encoded then encrypted; decryption only happens in get_decrypted_* / prepare_secrets_for_execution, not during list. 'AES' wording is loose (Fernet) but encryption-at-rest holds.

user_story: As a user, I want to replace a stored file secret, so that I can rotate certificates or update config files.
expected_behavior: Submits secret_id and optionally new file/description/target; replaces content (base64+encrypt) if new file else metadata only.
validation_notes: update_file_secret replaces content (base64+encrypt, updates filename/size/mime) when a new file is provided, else updates only description/target metadata; enforces secret_type=='file'.

user_story: As a user, I want to update secret values in stack instance variables, so that I can change deployment-time configuration.
expected_behavior: Submits variable name and new value; finds active stack instance, updates variable (flat or nested under module path). NotFoundError if stack/variable missing.
validation_notes: update_stack_variable_secret finds latest non-destroyed StackInstance and updates the named variable (flat or nested under module path) with the new value; NotFoundError if stack or variable missing.

user_story: As a user, I want to update stored value secrets, so that I can rotate API keys or change passwords.
expected_behavior: Submits secret_id and optionally new value/description/target; encrypts new value if provided, updates metadata.
validation_notes: update_value_secret re-encrypts the value when provided and updates description/target metadata; enforces secret_type=='value'.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to create manual snapshots of cluster config before risky operations, so that I can rollback if needed.
expected_behavior: Creates snapshot capturing current cluster config (CRDs + module variables). Returns snapshot ID with metadata (resource/module count, timestamp).
validation_notes: snapshots.py:create_snapshot (require_project_owner) -> snapshot_service.create_snapshot captures CRDs + module_config and records resource_count/module_count/timestamp.

user_story: As an admin, I want to delete old snapshots, so that I can manage storage and keep only relevant snapshots.
expected_behavior: Deletes snapshot record and associated config data. Requires admin role.
validation_notes: snapshots.py:delete_snapshot gated by require_admin; delegates to snapshot_service.delete_snapshot and returns 404 if missing.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to compare two snapshots, so that I can see what configuration changed between them.
expected_behavior: Diffs two snapshots and returns added/removed/modified resources with human-readable diff summaries.
validation_notes: snapshots.py:diff_snapshots -> snapshot_service.diff_snapshots reuses config_export diff_configs returning added/removed/modified resources.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to list and view snapshot details, so that I can understand snapshot content and find rollback targets.
expected_behavior: Lists snapshots per project (paginated, newest first) with metadata. Gets full snapshot detail including config data for inspection.
validation_notes: snapshots.py:list_project_snapshots (paginated, newest-first via service) and get_snapshot (includes config_data) match documented behavior.

user_story: As an admin, I want to restore a cluster from a snapshot, so that I can rollback after failed changes.
expected_behavior: Re-applies all CRD resources from snapshot via server-side apply. Module state is not modified. Requires admin role due to destructive nature.
validation_notes: snapshots.py:restore_snapshot gated by require_admin; snapshot_service.restore_snapshot re-applies CRDs via server-side apply (field_manager bnk-forge-snapshot-restore) without touching module state.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to test all SSH credentials at once, so that I can identify connectivity issues across the board.
expected_behavior: Tests every credential in parallel, persists per-credential results, returns passed/failed summary.
validation_notes: test_all_credentials fans out test_credential across a capped ThreadPoolExecutor (each worker uses its own SessionLocal), persists last_test_* per row, and returns {tested, results} per-credential summary.

user_story: As an operator, I want to create reusable SSH credentials, so that I can share secure access across clusters/projects.
expected_behavior: Submits name, host, port (default 22), username, auth_type (key/password), secrets; encrypts secrets, creates SSHCredential. Error on duplicate name.
validation_notes: create_credential rejects duplicate name (BadRequestError), defaults port 22 and auth_type 'key', manages single default, encrypts password/private_key/key_passphrase, and persists the SSHCredential.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove SSH credentials, so that I can clean up unused ones.
expected_behavior: Deletes record, returns 204. Error if not found.
validation_notes: delete_credential hard-deletes the row (NotFoundError if missing) and route returns 204; it additionally blocks deletion with BadRequestError when clusters/projects reference it (a safety superset of the documented behavior).

user_story: As a viewer, I want to inspect a specific SSH credential, so that I can verify its configuration.
expected_behavior: Returns single credential with full metadata and connectivity test results. Never returns actual secrets.
validation_notes: get_credential → serialize returns full metadata plus last_test_status/at/message and has_password/has_private_key flags, never the secrets.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all SSH credentials, so that I can select one for cluster configuration.
expected_behavior: Returns all sorted by is_default desc then name; includes host/port/username/auth_type/has_password/has_private_key/is_default/clusters_count/projects_count/last_test_status.
validation_notes: list_credentials orders by is_default desc then name and serializes host/port/username/auth_type/has_password/has_private_key/is_default/clusters_count/projects_count/last_test_status.

user_story: As an operator, I want to discover Kubernetes cluster info via SSH, so that I can retrieve kubeconfig without manual copy-paste.
expected_behavior: SSH into host, tries multiple kubeconfig locations (kubectl config view --raw, ~/.kube/config, /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf), returns base64 kubeconfig and discovered contexts. Error if SSH fails or none found.
validation_notes: probe_kubeconfig SSHes in (key or password), uses fetch_flattened_kubeconfig_over_ssh (oc/kubectl/raw cat ladder covering kubectl config view --raw, ~/.kube/config, /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf), returns base64 kubeconfig + parsed contexts, errors on SSH/parse failure. Needs live host.

user_story: As an operator, I want to bootstrap key-based SSH using a temporary password, so that I can switch to key auth without storing passwords.
expected_behavior: Connects via password, generates Ed25519 keypair, installs public key in authorized_keys, verifies key auth, stores credential with private key only (password NOT stored). Error if password auth fails.
validation_notes: setup_credential → SSHService.setup_key_auth connects with password, generates Ed25519 keypair, installs the public key in authorized_keys, verifies key auth, and stores only the private key (password discarded); BadRequestError if password auth denied. Needs live host.

user_story: As an operator, I want to verify SSH credentials work, so that I can ensure connectivity before deploying.
expected_behavior: Decrypts stored credentials, attempts SSH connection, returns success/failure. Persists last_test_status/at/message.
validation_notes: test_credential decrypts stored creds via the tunnel manager, attempts the connection, and persists last_test_status/at/message before returning the result. Needs a live SSH host to exercise.

user_story: As an operator, I want to modify SSH credentials, so that I can update details or rotate keys.
expected_behavior: Partial update of any field; encrypts new secrets, updates record. Error on duplicate name.
validation_notes: update_credential does partial update via model_dump(exclude_unset), re-encrypts provided password/private_key/key_passphrase, rejects duplicate name (BadRequestError), manages default, bumps updated_at.

user_story: As a user, I want to verify my project has all required secrets before deploying a stack, so that deployment doesn't fail due to missing credentials.
expected_behavior: Checks which project secrets the stack requires, returns lists of present vs missing secrets. Indicates which are blocking.
validation_notes: stacks.py:check_stack_prerequisites → stack_service.py:check_prerequisites delegates to StackDeploymentService.check_prerequisites, returning present vs missing required project secrets with blocking indicators.

feature: Create Project from Imported Blueprint Release
user_story: As a user, I want to create a new project directly from an imported blueprint release, so that I can quickly deploy a complete blueprint.
expected_behavior: Creates a new Project and instantiates modules from the blueprint manifest using provided inputs. Handles input inheritance from blueprint-level defaults.
validation_notes: stacks.py:create_project_from_imported_blueprint_release → imported_blueprint_service.py:create_project_from_release creates a Project and instantiates modules from the manifest, applying blueprint-level input defaults, credential-template inheritance, and explicit source mappings; blocks invalid/non-deployable releases and missing modules.

user_story: As a user, I want to create a stack instance from a template in my project, so that I can begin the deployment process.
expected_behavior: Creates a StackInstance with template_id, name, variables. Returns new instance with status=pending and empty module_instances array.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:create_instance creates a StackInstance with template_id/name/variables, status=PENDING, deployed_modules=[] (empty), and total_steps from the template module count.

user_story: As a user, I want to destroy a stack instance, so that its resources are cleaned up and the stack is removed from my project.
expected_behavior: Destroys all modules in reverse dependency order. Can force delete even if modules still have resources. Updates status to 'destroyed'.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:delete_stack force-deletes all stack modules when force=True, otherwise routes infrastructure modules through StackDeploymentService.destroy_stack (reverse-dependency event-chain destroy); SSH/ansible/not-initialized modules are deleted directly.

user_story: As a user, I want to start deploying a stack instance, so that the infrastructure defined in the template is created.
expected_behavior: Transitions instance to 'deploying'. Creates ProjectModule records for each template module. Queues modules for deployment in dependency order.
validation_notes: stacks.py:deploy_stack → stack_service.py:deploy_stack blocks during upgrades, then delegates to StackDeploymentService.deploy_stack which creates ProjectModule records and queues them in dependency order; returns status/current_step/total_steps.

user_story: As an operator, I want to duplicate an existing stack template, so that I can create variations without starting from scratch.
expected_behavior: Creates a new StackTemplate with copied definition but unique slug/name. Allows setting new name, description, category.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:duplicate_template copies the original definition into a new StackTemplate with a unique slug (_generate_unique_slug) and a new name; description/category default from the original or request.

user_story: As an operator, I want to export a stack template as JSON, so that I can share or version control the template.
expected_behavior: Returns the template definition as JSON including modules, variables, prerequisites, metadata for import/backup.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:export_template returns the full definition (modules, variable_templates, prerequisites, metadata) plus export_version/export_date as JSON.

feature: Get Imported Blueprint Release as Stack Template
user_story: As a user, I want to view an imported blueprint release in stack template format, so that I can use blueprints through the same interface as stack templates.
expected_behavior: Returns an imported BlueprintRelease in StackTemplateResponse shape with slug=release-{release_id}.
validation_notes: stacks.py:get_imported_blueprint_release → imported_blueprint_service.py:get_template_like returns the release in StackTemplateResponse shape with slug=release-{release_id}.

user_story: As a user, I want to see what inputs an imported blueprint requires, so that I can prepare values before deployment.
expected_behavior: Returns required and optional inputs from blueprint manifest with type, description, example, default, validation. Sorts by author-specified order.
validation_notes: imported_blueprint_service.py:get_required_inputs returns required+optional inputs with type/description/example/default/validation, applies manifest defaults, and sorts by author-specified 'order' (inputs without order fall to the end in original sequence).

user_story: As a user, I want to check the current status of a stack deployment, so that I can see progress and any errors.
expected_behavior: Returns overall status (pending/in_progress/success/failed), module-by-module status, current step, error messages for failed modules.
validation_notes: stacks.py:get_stack_status → stack_service.py:get_stack_status reconciles stale in-progress rows then returns deployment_service.get_deployment_status with overall + per-module status and error messages.

user_story: As a user, I want to view details of a specific stack instance, so that I can understand its configuration and deployment status.
expected_behavior: Returns instance with all inputs, module_instances array showing per-module deployment status, and deployment history with timestamps.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:get_instance returns the instance with variables, a module_instances array (per-module status/order/error/engine metadata), and timestamps (started_at/completed_at/created_at/updated_at).

user_story: As a user, I want to see what variables I need to provide for a stack template, so that I can prepare inputs before deployment.
expected_behavior: Returns required and optional inputs with name, type, description, example, default, validation rules, and whether value comes from project secrets or module outputs.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:get_required_inputs returns required+optional inputs with name/type/description/example/default/validation, attaches catalog-backed options (DOCA, external Helm charts), pre-populates from project context, and dedups across modules.

user_story: As a user, I want to view detailed information about a stack template, so that I can understand what it deploys before instantiating it.
expected_behavior: Returns full definition: name, description, category, cloud_provider, modules array, variable_templates, prerequisites, tags, maturity, deployment outcomes.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:get_template returns the full definition: name/description/category/cloud_provider, modules (with engine/capability metadata), variable_templates, prerequisites, tags, maturity, outcomes.

user_story: As an operator, I want to import a stack template from JSON, so that I can restore or share stack definitions.
expected_behavior: Accepts JSON template definition, creates a new StackTemplate. Validates structure and generates unique slug.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:import_template validates presence of name+modules, generates a unique slug, and creates a StackTemplate (created_by=user, is_public=False).

user_story: As a user, I want to see all stack instances in my project, so that I can monitor and manage active stacks.
expected_behavior: Returns paginated instances with status (pending/deploying/deployed/failed), template info, created timestamp, deployment progress summary.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:list_instances returns project stack instances filterable by status, ordered by created_at desc; StackInstanceResponse carries status/template/progress fields.

user_story: As a user, I want to see all available stack templates, so that I can find a starting point for my deployment.
expected_behavior: Returns paginated templates filterable by category, cloud_provider, tags, is_featured, created_by, is_public. Includes name, description, icon, estimated time/cost, difficulty, module count.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:list_templates filters by category/cloud_provider/tags/is_featured/created_by/is_public and orders by featured+name; StackTemplateListResponse includes name/description/icon/estimated time/cost/difficulty/module count.

user_story: As a user, I want to see what modules will be created from an imported blueprint, so that I can understand the deployment before committing.
expected_behavior: Returns modules array from blueprint manifest with name, description, dependencies. Shows total_modules, prerequisites, estimated cost/time.
validation_notes: imported_blueprint_service.py:preview_release returns the modules array (name/description/dependencies via get_template_like serialization) with total_modules, prerequisites, and estimated cost/time; no modules are created.

user_story: As a user, I want to see what modules will be created from a stack template, so that I can understand the deployment architecture before committing.
expected_behavior: Returns modules array with name, description, dependencies, estimated resource counts. Does not create any actual modules.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:preview_template returns the serialized modules (with catalog availability), prerequisites, estimated cost/time, and total_modules without creating any modules.

user_story: As an operator, I want to publish a stack template to the public marketplace, so that other users can discover and use it.
expected_behavior: Sets is_public flag true/false. Public templates appear in marketplace. Can toggle at any time.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:publish_template sets is_public true/false; system templates cannot be unpublished (ForbiddenError) but can otherwise be toggled at any time.

user_story: As a user, I want to execute all deployment steps (init + apply) for a stack, so that my infrastructure is fully provisioned.
expected_behavior: Executes init and apply for all stack modules in dependency order. Tracks per-module progress. Returns final status with any errors.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:run_deploy queues init+apply tasks for all stack modules in dependency order (deferring modules with unsatisfied deps), re-applies changed/applied modules (S18-001), runs pre-flight secret/cluster checks, and returns final status with queued/skipped/total counts and errors.

user_story: As a user, I want to save my project's current module configuration as a reusable stack template, so that others can deploy the same configuration.
expected_behavior: Captures current module configuration, variable defaults, metadata, creates a StackTemplate. Marks non-public by default.
validation_notes: stack_service.py:save_project_as_template captures the project's ordered ProjectModules (path/name/variables), metadata, and defaults into a new StackTemplate with is_public=False by default; errors if the project has no modules.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see state status for all modules in a project, so that I can understand which modules have deployed infrastructure.
expected_behavior: Lists all project modules with state existence, encryption status, resource/output counts, serial, lineage. Results cached for performance.
validation_notes: state_viewer.py:get_project_modules_with_state lists modules with state_exists/is_encrypted/resource_count/output_count/serial/lineage; cached 60s, skip_cache override.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all resources in a module's state and their dependencies, so that I can understand infrastructure relationships.
expected_behavior: Lists resources grouped by type/provider, shows counts, gets resource details with dependencies/dependents, builds dependency graph.
validation_notes: state_viewer.py:get_module_resources (counts_by_type/provider), get_resource_details (dependencies/dependents), get_dependency_graph (nodes/edges) via TerraformStateParser.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to refresh state info or reset state when it's stale, so that I can recover from state/code mismatches.
expected_behavior: Refresh re-reads state from disk; Reset deletes state directory, clears module status/outputs, logs operation. Reset is destructive and clears caches.
validation_notes: state_viewer.py:refresh_module_state re-parses from disk; reset_module_state (require_module_owner) rmtree's state dir, resets status/outputs, invalidates caches, logs.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see Terraform outputs from module state, so that I can access exported values.
expected_behavior: Returns outputs from state file with sensitive values masked as '***SENSITIVE***'.
validation_notes: state_viewer.py:get_module_outputs masks sensitive output values as '***SENSITIVE***' before returning.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to view parsed Terraform state for a module, so that I can see deployed resources and outputs.
expected_behavior: Parses state file (unencrypted or OpenTofu 1.8+ encrypted), returns resources, outputs, dependencies, metadata. Handles missing/invalid state gracefully.
validation_notes: state_viewer.py:get_module_state handles missing state (200 exists:false), encrypted (decrypt_state_async with DB-output fallback on failure), and unencrypted (TerraformStateParser), surfacing resources/outputs/deps/metadata.

user_story: As an operator, I want to configure alert notification channels, so that I can stay informed of platform issues
expected_behavior: Configure email/webhook/Slack alert destinations with testing capability.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx alerts tab renders components/settings/AlertChannels for email/webhook/Slack destinations with test capability.

user_story: As a user, I want to customize the UI appearance (theme), so that I can work in a preferred visual style
expected_behavior: Theme selector (light/dark) with live preview.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx appearance tab provides light/dark theme switch with a Current Theme preview badge driven by setTheme.

user_story: As an administrator, I want to view audit logs of all user actions, so that I can track changes for compliance
expected_behavior: Searchable log of user actions with timestamps, user info, action type, affected resource.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx audit tab renders components/settings/AuditLog (searchable user-action log).

user_story: As an administrator, I want to backup and restore platform data, so that I can protect against data loss
expected_behavior: Backup trigger and download. Restore upload and confirmation dialog.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx backup tab renders components/settings/BackupPanel for backup download and restore upload/confirmation.

user_story: As an administrator, I want to manage platform containers and services, so that I can control deployments
expected_behavior: View and manage forge service containers with start/stop/restart controls.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx monitor tab renders components/settings/ContainerManagement for forge service container controls.

user_story: As a system administrator, I want to manage database operations, so that I can maintain platform data integrity
expected_behavior: Database maintenance tools including backups, optimization, and integrity checks.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx monitor tab renders components/settings/DatabaseManagement for DB maintenance tools.

user_story: As a system administrator, I want to monitor system resource usage and performance metrics, so that I can optimize deployments
expected_behavior: Dashboard showing CPU, memory, disk, network metrics with historical charts.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx monitor tab renders components/settings/PerformanceMonitor metrics dashboard.

user_story: As an administrator, I want to configure system-wide defaults, so that I can standardize platform behavior
expected_behavior: Settings for default credentials, timeouts, resource limits, and other global configuration.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx defaults tab renders components/settings/SystemDefaults for global default configuration.

user_story: As an administrator, I want to upgrade the platform to newer versions, so that I can access new features and fixes
expected_behavior: Shows current version, available upgrades, release notes, and upgrade action with progress monitoring.
validation_notes: pages/System.tsx monitor tab renders components/settings/SystemUpgrade showing version/available upgrades/progress.

user_story: As a dashboard viewer, I want to monitor backend process CPU, memory, network usage in real-time, so that I can spot performance issues.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/process-metrics (public, no auth) returns CPU%, memory (RSS/VMS), thread count, file descriptors, network bytes (cumulative since start); frontend diffs samples to compute rates.
validation_notes: system.py:get_process_metrics is on public_router (no auth) returning cpu_percent, rss/vms, num_threads, open_fds, cumulative net_rx/tx bytes and sampled_at for client-side rate diffing.

user_story: As an operator, I want to restart BNK Forge services (backend, workers, frontend), so that I can apply changes or recover from issues.
expected_behavior: POST /api/system/containers/restart with services array restarts Docker containers; fails safely if db/redis in request; warns that backend restart may disconnect API.
validation_notes: system.py:restart_containers (admin) rejects postgres/redis with RESTRICTED_SERVICE, validates names, restarts via docker, warns backend restart may disconnect API.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see the status of all BNK Forge Docker containers, so that I can verify all services are running.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/containers/status returns list of containers with state (running/stopped), status string (e.g., 'Up 2 hours').
validation_notes: system.py:get_container_status (admin) lists bnk-forge containers with status string and running/stopped state via docker ps.

user_story: As a DBA, I want to clean up old records by type (e.g., logs >30 days old), so that I can reduce database size.
expected_behavior: POST /api/system/database/cleanup with cleanup_type and older_than_days deletes old records by type; returns deleted count.
validation_notes: system.py:cleanup_database -> system_service.cleanup_database (admin) deletes by cleanup_type/older_than_days and returns deleted count (also enforces a 7-day floor).

user_story: As a DBA, I want to see database table sizes and row counts, so that I can monitor database growth.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/database/stats returns table-level stats: row count, size in bytes; total database size.
validation_notes: system.py:get_database_stats -> system_service.get_database_stats returns per-table rows/size_mb plus total database size_mb.

user_story: As a DBA, I want to run VACUUM ANALYZE on the database, so that I can optimize query performance.
expected_behavior: POST /api/system/database/vacuum runs VACUUM ANALYZE; returns operation status.
validation_notes: system.py:vacuum_database -> system_service.vacuum_database (admin) runs VACUUM ANALYZE in AUTOCOMMIT and returns status/duration.

user_story: As a developer, I want to check MCP (Model Context Protocol) server health and see available tools, so that I can debug MCP integrations.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/mcp/status (admin) probes MCP via JSON-RPC ping, fetches tools/list, groups tools by module; returns status (healthy/degraded/offline), latency_ms, tool_catalog grouped by category.
validation_notes: system.py:get_mcp_status (admin) probes MCP via JSON-RPC ping, performs initialize handshake + tools/list, groups tools by module, returns status/latency_ms/tool_catalog.

user_story: As an operator, I want to view held module locks and force-release stale locks, so that I can recover from hung workers.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/workspaces/locks lists all held locks (module_id, holding_task_id, heartbeat_at); GET /{project_id}/{module_id} checks specific lock; DELETE force-releases lock (admin escape hatch).
validation_notes: system.py list/check/force-release workspace lock endpoints (admin) expose module_id/holding_task_id/heartbeat_at via ModuleLockService; DELETE force-releases as admin escape hatch.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see application performance metrics, so that I can track system efficiency.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/performance returns metrics aggregated from recent tasks: success rate, average duration, error counts.
validation_notes: system.py:get_performance_metrics -> system_service aggregates recent-task avg duration, failed counts and longest-running task.

user_story: As an operator, I want to verify that a system upgrade completed successfully, so that I can confirm all services are healthy.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/upgrade/verify runs detailed checks: service health, version changed, migrations applied; returns verification results.
validation_notes: system.py:verify_post_upgrade -> system_service runs version/database/redis/celery/migration checks and returns verdict with per-check results.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see recent failed tasks and errors, so that I can troubleshoot issues.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/errors returns recent failed/errored tasks with error messages and timestamps.
validation_notes: system.py:get_recent_errors -> system_service.get_recent_errors returns recent FAILED tasks with error and timestamp.

user_story: As an admin, I want to view and configure system defaults (e.g., default timeouts, resource limits), so that I can customize platform behavior.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/defaults returns all defaults by category; GET /status checks if required defaults configured; PUT /defaults and PUT /{key} update batch/single.
validation_notes: system.py exposes GET /defaults, GET /defaults/status, PUT /defaults (batch) and PUT /defaults/{key} (single) delegating to defaults_service.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check overall system health including database, redis, and worker status, so that I can diagnose issues.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/health (public, no auth) returns component status (backend, database, redis, celery) with response times and warnings (e.g., no workers available).
validation_notes: system.py:get_system_health is on public_router (no auth) and system_service.get_health reports backend/database/redis/celery status, response times, and 'No workers available' warning.

user_story: As an admin, I want to check if the system is in maintenance mode, so that I know if backup/restore is in progress.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/maintenance (public, no auth) returns maintenance_mode boolean, message, started_at; returns 503 on all other requests when active.
validation_notes: system.py:get_maintenance_mode is public (no auth) returning maintenance_mode/message/started_at; maintenance_middleware.py returns 503 for all non-allowlisted paths when active.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check the status of an ongoing system upgrade, so that I can recover state after page refresh or reconnection.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/upgrade/status returns last/current upgrade state from DB with status (none/in_progress/completed/interrupted), phase, progress, started_at, eta.
validation_notes: system.py:get_upgrade_status reads persisted DB state and downgrades stale in_progress to 'interrupted' when no upgrade running; returns status/phase/progress/started_at.

user_story: As an operator, I want to check the current system version and upgrade readiness, so that I can plan platform upgrades.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/version returns current version, available versions, upgrade_readiness (warnings, blockers); checks worker health, running tasks, pending jobs.
validation_notes: system.py:get_system_version merges get_system_version + get_upgrade_readiness (worker/running-task/docker checks) into the version + upgrade_readiness response.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see queue depth and worker metrics, so that I can monitor throughput and identify bottlenecks.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/queue-metrics returns queue stats (pending, active tasks per queue), worker count (total, active, offline), completed tasks last hour.
validation_notes: system.py:get_queue_metrics -> system_service returns per-queue pending/active, worker total/active/offline and completed_last_hour.

user_story: As an admin, I want to trigger a system upgrade with live output streaming via WebSocket, so that I can monitor upgrade progress.
expected_behavior: POST /api/system/upgrade starts async upgrade process; streams output via WebSocket subscription; returns initial status and task info.
validation_notes: system.py:trigger_system_upgrade -> system_service.trigger_upgrade runs safety pre-checks then spawns a daemon thread publishing progress to the WebSocket Redis channel.

user_story: As a DBA, I want to view workspace statistics, find orphaned workspaces, and clean them up, so that I can manage persistent directories.
expected_behavior: GET /api/system/workspaces/stats returns workspace count, total size; GET /orphaned lists orphaned workspaces; POST /cleanup deletes orphaned ones.
validation_notes: system.py workspace stats/orphaned/cleanup endpoints (admin) delegate to WorkspaceManager returning count/size, orphaned list, and deleted_count on cleanup.

user_story: As an operator, I want to view all deployment operations with filters and details, so that I can audit and troubleshoot changes
expected_behavior: Sidebar with status filters (completed/running/failed/queued), type filters (init/plan/apply/destroy/helm/k8s operations), project filter, quick stats. Table showing task details, status, type, project, module, timestamps. Expandable task detail with full logs.
validation_notes: pages/TaskHistory.tsx provides status/type/project filters, quick stats, task table and expandable detail with logs.

user_story: As an operator, I want to cancel a running or queued task, so that I can stop stuck operations.
expected_behavior: POST /api/tasks/{id}/cancel sends SIGTERM to Celery task; updates status to 'cancelled'; releases workspace lock; reverts module state if applicable; publishes WebSocket update.
validation_notes: tasks.py:cancel_task revokes Celery with SIGTERM, sets status cancelled, force-releases workspace lock, reverts in-flight module state, and publishes a WebSocket task update.

user_story: As a DBA, I want to delete old completed tasks to free up database space, so that I can reduce database size.
expected_behavior: DELETE /api/tasks/cleanup with older_than_days (default 60) deletes tasks with status completed/failed/cancelled created before cutoff; returns deleted_count.
validation_notes: tasks.py:cleanup_old_tasks deletes completed/failed/cancelled tasks older than days (default 60) and returns deleted_count.

user_story: As an operator, I want to view detailed information about a specific task including logs, so that I can troubleshoot failures.
expected_behavior: GET /api/tasks/{id} returns full task record with logs (truncated if >log_max_size or log_tail specified); logs_truncated boolean indicates if output was truncated.
validation_notes: tasks.py:get_task truncates logs by log_tail or log_max_size and sets logs_truncated accordingly.

user_story: As an operator, I want to see task statistics (counts by status/type, average duration), so that I can monitor system throughput.
expected_behavior: GET /api/tasks/stats/summary returns totals by status and type, average duration; optional project_id filter; period configurable (1-90 days, default 7).
validation_notes: tasks.py:get_task_stats returns by_status/by_type counts and average_duration via SQL GROUP BY with optional project_id and days(1-90,default 7).

user_story: As an operator, I want to view task history with pagination and filtering, so that I can track background job progress.
expected_behavior: GET /api/tasks returns paginated tasks (default 50, max 200) with filters: project_id, module_id, status, task_type; ordered by created_at desc; includes project_name and module_name via eager load.
validation_notes: tasks.py:get_tasks paginates (default 50/max 200) with project_id/module_id/status/task_type filters, ordered created_at desc, eager-loads project_name and module_name.

user_story: As a dashboard client, I want to receive real-time task status updates via WebSocket, so that I see progress without polling.
expected_behavior: WS /api/tasks/ws/tasks accepts client connections; receives task_update messages with status, project_id, module_id, error; ping/pong keepalive; 60s idle timeout.
validation_notes: tasks.py:websocket_task_updates accepts clients, echoes pong on 'ping', has 60s idle timeout; task_update messages published via ws_manager carry status/project_id/module_id/error.

user_story: As an administrator, I want to manage user accounts and roles, so that I can control platform access
expected_behavior: Admin-only page listing all users with roles (admin/operator/viewer), email, active status, project count. Create, edit, delete users with role assignment.
validation_notes: pages/UserManagement.tsx is admin-gated (useRole), lists users with role/email/active/project-count and provides create/edit/delete with role assignment.

feature: Apply Variable Mapping Template to Module
user_story: As a module owner, I want to apply a template to my module, so that I can quickly configure common variable mappings.
expected_behavior: User specifies template ID. System iterates template.mappings, creates VariableMapping for each mapping (skips if source already mapped). Increments template.usage_count. Returns created/skipped counts.
validation_notes: apply_variable_mapping_template in routes/project_variable_mappings.py iterates template.mappings, creates a VariableMapping per mapping (skipping already-mapped sources), increments usage_count, and returns created/skipped counts.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to map external source variables to internal module variables with optional transformation, so that I can adapt variable naming and format.
expected_behavior: User creates mapping specifying source/target variable names and transform type. System checks for duplicates, creates VariableMapping record. Returns mapping ID and metadata.
validation_notes: create_variable_mapping in routes/project_variable_mappings.py checks for duplicate source, creates the VariableMapping with transform type, and returns mapping ID and metadata.

user_story: As an operator, I want to create a reusable variable mapping template, so that other users can apply it to their modules.
expected_behavior: Operator creates template with name, description, array of mapping definitions, and is_public flag. System checks for duplicate names. Returns template ID.
validation_notes: create_variable_mapping_template in routes/project_variable_mappings.py checks duplicate names, stores the mappings array as JSON with is_public, and returns the template ID.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to remove a variable mapping, so that I can undo previous wiring.
expected_behavior: User deletes mapping by ID. System removes VariableMapping record. Returns success confirmation.
validation_notes: delete_variable_mapping in routes/project_variable_mappings.py deletes by ID with module_id validation and returns a success response.

user_story: As an operator, I want to remove an obsolete mapping template, so that I can keep the template catalog clean.
expected_behavior: Operator deletes template by ID. System removes VariableMappingTemplate record. Returns success confirmation.
validation_notes: delete_variable_mapping_template in routes/project_variable_mappings.py removes the template by ID and returns a success response.

user_story: As a user, I want to see the schema and current overrides for a module's variables, so that I can understand what configuration is available.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns module.variable_overrides (user-set values), module.library_module.variables_schema (available variables with type/description/required/default). Filters out platform variables.
validation_notes: get_module_variables in services/project_module_service.py returns module.variable_overrides plus library_module.variables_schema, filtering out platform variables.

user_story: As a viewer, I want to see all project-level variables (user-set, auto-discovered, configurable), so that I understand what values will be injected into modules.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns: stored_vars (user-set), discovered_vars (from deployed module outputs ordered by deployment_order), configurable (from module schemas grouped by module). Caches result for 60s. Includes value_source for each variable (user/discovered/default/unset).
validation_notes: get_project_variables in services/project_service.py returns stored_vars, discovered_vars (deployed module outputs ordered by deployment_order), and configurable schema vars grouped by module with value_source, caching the result ~60s.

user_story: As a user, I want to see common default values used across project modules, so that I understand what values will be injected.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns common_defaults (static: VPC CIDRs, resource names, sizing, booleans, AZs) and custom_defaults (from project.project_variables). Returns effective merged defaults.
validation_notes: get_variable_defaults in routes/project_variables.py returns static common_defaults (CIDRs, names, sizing, booleans, AZs) merged with custom_defaults from project.project_variables.

user_story: As a user, I want to browse reusable variable mapping templates, so that I can apply common mapping patterns to multiple modules.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns list of public VariableMappingTemplate records with name, description, mappings array, usage count, and creation time.
validation_notes: get_variable_mapping_templates in routes/project_variable_mappings.py returns public VariableMappingTemplate records with name, description, mappings array, usage count, and creation time.

user_story: As a user, I want to see all variable mappings for a module (source -> target transformations), so that I understand input wiring.
expected_behavior: Endpoint returns list of VariableMapping records for a module with source/target names, transform type (none/uppercase/lowercase/json_encode/base64), active status, and description.
validation_notes: get_variable_mappings in routes/project_variable_mappings.py returns the module's VariableMapping records with source/target, transform type (none/uppercase/lowercase/json_encode/base64), active status, and description.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to reset defaults back to common defaults, so that I remove all project-specific overrides.
expected_behavior: User resets defaults. System removes variable_defaults from project.project_variables. Returns success confirmation.
validation_notes: reset_variable_defaults in routes/project_variables.py removes variable_defaults from project.project_variables, flags the column modified, and returns success.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to set project-wide variables that will be injected into all module deployments, so that modules receive required shared configuration.
expected_behavior: User updates variables dict. System stores as project.project_variables (flat structure). Invalidates cache. Returns variables_count and updated variables.
validation_notes: update_project_variables in routes/project_variables.py stores the variables dict flat in project.project_variables, invalidates the cache, and returns variables_count plus updated variables.

user_story: As a project owner, I want to customize default values for my project, so that all modules use project-specific defaults.
expected_behavior: User updates defaults dict (CIDRs, names, sizing). System stores in project.project_variables['variable_defaults']. Returns updated defaults count.
validation_notes: update_variable_defaults in routes/project_variables.py stores the defaults dict under project.project_variables['variable_defaults'] and returns the updated defaults count.

user_story: As a module owner, I want to modify a variable mapping, so that I can adjust wiring configuration.
expected_behavior: User updates mapping by ID with new source/target/transform. System validates and persists changes. Returns updated mapping.
validation_notes: update_variable_mapping in routes/project_variable_mappings.py updates source/target/transform by ID, validates, persists, and returns the updated mapping.

user_story: As an operator, I want to modify a mapping template, so that I can keep shared templates current.
expected_behavior: Operator updates template name/description/mappings/visibility. System validates unique name (excluding self). Returns updated template.
validation_notes: update_variable_mapping_template in routes/project_variable_mappings.py updates name/description/mappings/visibility and validates unique name excluding self before returning the updated template.

user_story: As a user, I want to validate variable values against a module's schema before deploying, so that I catch configuration errors early.
expected_behavior: User provides module library ID and variables dict. System checks against module.variables_schema (required/type/sensitive constraints). Returns validation success, errors, and warnings for unknown variables.
validation_notes: validate_variables in services/project_module_service.py checks the supplied variables against variables_schema (required/type/sensitive) via VariableValidator and returns success, errors, and warnings for unknown variables.
